Ironclad Inquiries · Case 3 · One-shot

The Sleeper Under Bagathorn

A convict sent home in shackles, giants waiting at the mine mouth, and a mountain that has started, very slowly, to wake up.

Ironclad one-shot · level 12 · 3 PCs ~4 hours 2 core fights + 2 optional Spotlight: Boon Orek Vali

sections.title: Before the session
sections.html:
The case file

A one-shot has no recap. Give the table these three facts before the cold open:

  • Ironclad Inquiries is a multi-planar detective agency run from the Nexus, a pocket dimension between planes. Its Director, Seraphine Nightshade, sends Detectives through a gate to cases anywhere. Clients pay for results and discretion, not ethics.
  • Boon Gultor is serving a life sentence. Ironclad has him on "work release": a magical bracelet tracks him, and between cases he goes back to the cells. Orek and Vali are hired Detectives.
  • Boon grew up in Bagathorn, a dwarven mining town, in the family that has advised its mayors for generations. He left in chains after one of his bombs killed miners. He hasn't been back.

Decide before you run

  • Where Bagathorn is [OPEN]. Proposal: the mountain arc on Ekenda's east side, off Talor. Boon's backstory spells it "Bagathron" once; this page uses Bagathorn.
  • Dorn sabotaged Boon's old bomb new. It's the big reveal in Scene 4. A softer version (Dorn saw the flaw and stayed silent) is a one-line swap in the journal handout.
  • Vali's patron. The Aegis Ward dims at his pact, and the Sleeper's dream flinches from it. Nothing more is named. Check with Eddy whether he wants that pulled on.
  • Corvane new, the Nexus Bazaar broker who sold Dorn the Hush charms, is set up as a series thread. Keep or cut the closing note.
  • The fee [OPEN]: this page assumes 4,000 gp to Ironclad and 600 gp to each Detective.

The night at a glance

Two set-piece fights (⚔): the Ninth Gallery and the climax. Two optional fights (⚔?) are ready in Scenes 2 and 4 if the table wants more. Scene 1 drops the party into Bagathorn at about 10 pm and hands out three leads. Scenes 2 to 4 play in any order. Scene 5 starts when the party follows Dorn down, or at clock 6, whichever comes first. Dawn ends it.

1 · Come Home, Detectives → 2 · The Court at the Mine Mouth ⚔? · 3 · The Ninth Gallery ⚔ · 4 · The House of Gultor ⚔? → 5 · The Sleeper Wakes ⚔ climax → Dawn

Spotlight tracker

Encounters at a glance

Two set-piece fights carry the session, each with battlefield twists that change round by round. Two optional fights are written up in full in collapsed boxes, ready if the table is hungry for more. XP uses the 2024 budgets for three level 12 PCs: Low 6,600 · Moderate 11,100 · High 14,100. Every monster is in Foundry's SRD compendium; reskins are noted on each card.

FightFoesXP · difficultyTwistsTime
⚔ Hunger in the Walls Scene 34 Xorns, then 2 Earth Elementals (the dream-guardians)10,800 · ModerateThe rescue steps happen mid-fight. Xorns swim through stone (tremorsense finds them), eat metal, and take gem bribes. The gallery floods and collapses round by round.~40 min
⚔ The Sleeper Wakes Scene 5Dorn, Stone-Wed + 2 Earth Elementals + the waking Sleeper9,500+ · High with lair actionsA round limit; four steps to win; tilting floor plates; a loose Eye rolling for the fissures; Dorn's phase change on a rising pillar; guardians that switch sides.~50 min
⚔? Kolgrim's Test Scene 2, optionalKolgrim (Stone Giant, 200 HP) + 3 Earth Elementals8,300 · Low–ModerateA ritual duel: fight inside the ring, he yields at half HP, and if you win he joins the climax.~25 min
⚔? The Hushed Scene 4, optional3 Assassins (Corvane's agents)11,700 · ModerateSilent attackers; tremorsense beats the Hush; the stone takes Dorn in round 3.~25 min

With both core fights you're at about 35% combat. Add one optional fight for about 45%, or both for about half the session.

Battle map prompts

Each fight's location (including the optional ones) has a collapsed Battle map prompt (copper border) beside its art and soundtrack prompts. They're top-down, overhead and flat, with no people, creatures, lettering or modern objects, so they're ready for a VTT grid. Each prompt names a grid size: generate at that aspect ratio (add --ar in Midjourney), then set the scene's grid in Foundry to match. Every prompt starts with the same map style lock, so the maps look like one set:

Top-down orthographic fantasy battle map for a virtual tabletop, hand-painted digital illustration, lush and intricately detailed, saturated jewel-tone palette with deep contrasting shadows, dramatic glowing light sources casting colored pools of light, rich textures on stone, timber, moss and water, crisp readable shapes that stay clear under tokens, flat overhead view with no perspective tilt, medieval fantasy setting.

The party at a glance

PCRemember during play
Boon AndyDwarf Artillerist 12, criminal. Can't channel the weave through his body, so he casts through tools and objects. Eldritch Cannon, Flash of Genius (adds Int to an ally's check), expertise with thieves' and tinker's tools, Spell Sniper. Tremorsense 60 ft on stone, darkvision 120 ft. The work-release bracelet tracks him.
Orek ColinDwarf Battle Master 4 / Bladesinger 8. Hates being called a mage. Investigation +13, Arcana and History +9, jeweler's kit, smith's tools. Maneuvers: Disarming, Goading, Trip. Speaks Giant. Allergic to most metals (a rash after long contact). Tremorsense, darkvision 120 ft.
Vali EddyStone giant goliath, Vengeance paladin 8 / Fiend warlock 4. Speaks Giant. Large Form (1/LR), Stone's Endurance, Divine Sense, Aura of Protection +5, Vow of Enmity. Sun Blade, Repulsion Shield, Immovable Rod. Ashborn Legion war orphan; believes everyone answers for what they did.

Until dawn · the case clock

Ironclad cases run on a deadline, so this clock is visible and resolves during play. Each segment is about an hour. Tick it automatically as scenes end (Scene 1 +1, Scene 2 +1, Scene 3 +2, Scene 4 +1) and on the failure rows that say so. Click a segment to mark it (saved in this browser only).

2Midnight tremor. Lanterns swing and a lift-cage jams. If the trapped miners aren't out yet, their air is short: Scene 3 rescue DCs +2.
4The town panics. Chimneys fall on the lower tier; families climb toward the passes in the dark. Mayor Durrin decides to hand Boon to the giants at dawn and sends the militia looking for him.
6Dorn goes down on his own, sleepwalking, stone to the elbows. The giants' sealing wall cracks and Ammaskar's eyes open. Go to Scene 5 now.
7Kolgrim starts singing the mountain down, unless Thrunna was persuaded in Scene 2. Scene 5 loses one round.
8Dawn. Ammaskar sits up. The Gate opens in Lantern Square and Boon's bracelet recalls him. See "If dawn comes first" in Scene 5.

Series clocks

These carry into future Ironclad cases. Jot ticks during play, mark them after, and reveal the effects at the top of the next Ironclad one-shot. Triggers and effects are in the arc doc.

Items for Foundry

Every item the party can pick up has two buttons. Built for the dnd5e system 4.x or later (Foundry v12 and v13). Mechanics live in each item's description, with inline rolls; add an activity in Foundry if you want one-click automation.

Copy macro (fastest)

  • In Foundry, click an empty slot on the macro bar.
  • Set Type to Script and paste.
  • Click Execute. The item appears in the Items sidebar.

Foundry .json (Import Data)

  • Save the file (your browser asks first).
  • In the Items sidebar, create a blank item of the type shown on the card.
  • Right-click it → Import Data → choose the file.

Soundtrack prompts

Each scene has a collapsed soundtrack prompt for Suno, and the big turns (the giants rise, the Sleeper opens her eyes, the Gate at dawn) have extra cues. Every prompt starts with "An orchestral ambient soundtrack of…", names real orchestral instruments and rules out synths, pads and electronic sounds, asks for an instrumental track, and shows its length in characters so you can check it against your Suno plan's limit. The night moves from cold and mysterious in the Nexus, to heavy and earthbound at the mine, to intimate and sad in the Gultor house, to enormous at the end.

sections.title: Come Home, Detectives
sections.html:
1

Come Home, Detectives

Evening → 10 pmThe Nexus → Lantern Square, Bagathorn
Who: Director Seraphine Nightshade, Turnkey Nine, Bramm Gultor, Mayor Hesk Durrin, Fennick Gultor, the squareLeans on: Boon Orek Vali
Why they're here
  • A case has come in. Seraphine wants all three: Boon because the client asked for him by name, Orek and Vali because the giants at the mine mouth speak only Giant, and both of them do.

The scene's job: set the tone (noir, deadline), let Seraphine needle each PC once, drop them into a town that hates Boon, and hand out three leads. Clock starts at 0 when they arrive; +1 when the scene ends.

Art prompt · The Nexus, Grand Hall & the Aegis Ward

Painterly dark-fantasy concept art, deep-mountain noir, cold blue-grey granite and soot-black shadow cut by warm amber lantern light, veins of pale opalescent violet glowing in the stone, drifting rock dust in the air, cinematic composition, highly detailed environment, 16:9 aspect ratio. A vast interplanar great hall in perpetual twilight, its ceiling stripped away to reveal a sky of violet nebulae and slow rivers of gold stardust. Obsidian and old-stone architecture from a dozen worlds jammed together: gothic arches beside brass clockwork galleries, floating walkways that detach and drift between balconies. At the far end, a wide threshold shimmers behind a hanging curtain of silver liquid light, rippling like mercury, with tall void-glass doors dimly visible behind it. Brass desks heaped with case files, a rack of trench coats, an iron cage-lift rising from cells below, a single dropped manacle on the floor. Amber lamps on long chains, faint smoke, motes of stardust falling like slow snow. Mysterious, bureaucratic and a little dangerous. No people, no text, no watermark.

Art prompt · Lantern Square, Bagathorn at night

Painterly dark-fantasy concept art, deep-mountain noir, cold blue-grey granite and soot-black shadow cut by warm amber lantern light, veins of pale opalescent violet glowing in the stone, drifting rock dust in the air, cinematic composition, highly detailed environment, 16:9 aspect ratio. A dwarven mining town at night, carved in tiers up the shoulder of a huge dark mountain, seen from its central square. Squat stone houses with turf roofs and iron-banded doors stacked terrace above terrace, linked by steep stairways and creaking counterweighted lift-cages on chains. The square is paved with worn granite and ringed by tall iron lantern posts, every lantern swinging the same way, all at once. A stone well with a bronze bell frame; a toppled cart of coal; a crack running across the flagstones. High on the slope, a slim black basalt tower with a brass observatory dome; above it, a raw timber headframe against the stars; far up the flank, a red glow at the mouth of a mine. Dust sifting down from the eaves. Cold mountain night, breath-fog, uneasy. No people, no text, no watermark.

Soundtrack prompt · The Nexus

An orchestral ambient soundtrack of a secret interplanar detective agency at the end of a long night, performed by a live chamber orchestra: a smoky, wandering solo clarinet over muted strings, soft pizzicato double basses walking slowly, a lone muted trumpet answering from far away, high violin harmonics like starlight, and a ticking woodblock-and-celesta figure like a clock in another room. Noir, cool, mysterious, a little wry. 72 BPM, D Dorian. Real acoustic instruments, concert-hall reverb, no synthesizers, no pads, no electronic sounds. Loopable, instrumental, no vocals.

Cold open

Boon, they come for you at the end of the second shift, when the cells beneath the Nexus are quietest. Turnkey Nine, a warforged with a jailer's ring of keys welded to its wrist, unlocks the door without a word, the way it always does. The lift is an iron cage on a chain. It rises through forty feet of black stone, and the cold of the cells drains out of your bones as you climb, and the bracelet on your wrist gives one small click, the way it always does when you cross the line from prisoner to asset.

The cage opens onto the Grand Hall, and the Nexus hits you all at once. The ceiling isn't there. Where a roof should be, the Astral Sea spills overhead: violet nebulae, slow rivers of gold stardust, and every so often a mote of that stardust drifts down and lands on someone's hat. Walkways float loose between the balconies, detach, drift, and dock again somewhere else. The air has been breathed on a dozen planes before it reached you; it smells of ozone and parchment dust, clockwork grease, and somewhere underneath, faintly, blood. At the nearest desk a warforged in a trench coat is arguing in clipped binary with a djinni about travel expenses, and losing.

Orek. Vali. You were summoned from your quarters by a brass message-beetle that would not stop buzzing until you followed it, and it led you here, to this patch of floor, to the dwarf in shackles stepping out of the lift. Turnkey Nine unlocks the shackles and keeps them. It does not unlock the bracelet. Nobody ever unlocks the bracelet.

Above the far end of the hall, a curtain of silver light hangs across a threshold, rippling like poured mercury, and beyond it tall doors of black glass stand closed. A voice comes out of the air beside your ears, all three of you at once, cool and close as a whisper in a confessional.

"Detectives. Come up. All three of you. Bring the convict."

The Aegis Ward

The silver curtain reads each person's essence before it lets them through. Play each PC's moment, one at a time. No rolls.

Orek

The silver washes over you like cold water, and it sings: a clear, rising chime, the note the Ward gives for archmages. A clerk on a floating walkway looks up, impressed, and says, to nobody in particular, "Well. There's a real mage." The doors open in warm gold.

Vali

The light thins and dims around you, and for a breath it sputters a dull red, the way it does at shadow pacts, and you taste copper. Something in you has been read and noted. Then, grudgingly, the curtain turns gold. Nobody comments. Somebody, somewhere, writes something down.

Boon

The curtain finds the bracelet first. It flares, and a sigil you've seen a thousand times burns on the silver for a moment: a closed padlock inside a circle. In custody. The doors open anyway. The Ward has never cared what you did. It only cares who holds the key.

The Director

The Director's office is cold enough to fog your breath and so quiet you can hear the dust settle. A circular window fills the far wall, and beyond it the storms of the Elemental Plane of Air turn in silence: towers of grey cloud lit from inside by lightning that never makes a sound. The desk is a single slab of petrified weirwood, and behind it sits a woman you can't quite see. A veil of living shadow moves over her face like smoke over water. Her eyes are two pools of ink, and they are impossible to look away from, and they are impossible to lie to.

She turns a many-faceted gem in her gloved fingers. Light catches in it, splits, scatters across the ceiling in a hundred points. Then she closes her hand, and the light goes out.

"Bagathorn," says Director Seraphine Nightshade. "A dwarven mining town on a mountain called Thurn. Three nights ago a new shaft broke into something old. Two nights ago something was stolen from it. Tonight there are three stone giants sitting at the mouth of the mine, and the mountain has begun to shake." The ink-dark eyes move to Boon, and stay there. "The client is the hereditary consultant to Bagathorn's mayor. Bramm Gultor." A pause exactly long enough to land. "He asked for you by name, Mister Gultor. He paid extra."

Director Seraphine Nightshade
Director of Ironclad Inquiries · cool, pragmatic, always three moves ahead
Look
A veil of living shadow over her face; eyes like ink; gloves; a faceted gem she crushes the light out of
Voice
Quiet, dry, never hurried. Ends conversations by looking away.
Wants
The mountain still, the client grateful, and Ironclad's first door into the giants' deep roads
Hiding
She knows Bramm is lying by omission and suspects why. She took the job anyway.
In the field
She can speak into the Detectives' ears and watches their vitals. Use her two or three times tonight, no more. Lines in small caps are her voice in their ears.

"Results, Detectives. I don't need to know how. I would prefer not to."

Portrait prompt · Seraphine Nightshade (for an actor or token)

Painterly dark-fantasy character portrait, deep-mountain noir, cold blue-grey shadow cut by warm amber lamplight, drifting dust, highly detailed, 2:3 aspect ratio. A poised, ageless woman seated behind a desk of grey petrified wood, her face half hidden by a veil of living shadow that drifts like smoke over water, only her eyes clear: two pools of glossy black ink. High-collared charcoal coat with silver buttons, black leather gloves, one hand holding up a many-faceted pale gem that throws scattered points of light. Behind her, a round window onto silent grey storm clouds lit by soundless lightning. Cold breath-fog in the air. Composed, unreadable, dangerous. No text, no watermark.

Handout · Ironclad case card
CASE 3 · BAGATHORN (Mt. Thurn)
CLIENT: Bramm Gultor, Consultant to the Mayor
ITEM: unknown. "Something the giants want back."
DEADLINE: dawn (Gate reopens, Lantern Square)
DELIVER: the item to its owners; the thief to "the appropriate authority"
FEE: 4,000 gp to the agency
ASSETS: Gultor, B. (custody) · Opaldigger, O. · Vali
NOTE: Stone giants. Speak Giant. Do not speak first.

Three questions

Before she answers anything, Seraphine asks each of them one question. She listens, says nothing about the answer, and moves on.

Boon

"The town that put you in chains may be under the mountain by morning. Some men would call that justice. Are you some men?"

Orek

"The Ward sang for you the way it sings for archmages. My clerk called you a mage. I watched your jaw. What would you like to be called, Opaldigger?" (Whatever he answers, she uses it from now on.)

Vali

"The Ward dimmed for you. Something holds a claim on you, paladin, and it isn't a god. I don't care. But you believe everyone answers for what they did. Tonight you'll meet a family of people who have done things. Who will you make answer?"

Seraphine's answers · for the questions players will ask
They askSeraphine saysDM truth
What was stolen?"The client doesn't know, or won't say. The giants know. Ask them politely, in their language, and don't speak first."The Eye of Ammaskar (Scene 2).
Why did he ask for Boon?"He said, 'Send my son.' I don't ask clients why. I charge them for it."Bramm suspects Dorn and needs an outsider with the family name.
What happens at dawn?"The Gate opens in Lantern Square. The bracelet brings Mister Gultor home whether you've finished or not. I'd be standing near him."Hard stop. The clock's last segment.
What do we do with the thief?"The contract says 'the appropriate authority.' Ironclad has no opinion on which. Bring them back alive and I might have an opinion."She'll offer the thief work release (Dawn).
They'll blame Boon.She taps a ledger without looking at it. "Two nights ago, at the hour of the theft, Mister Gultor was in Cell Nineteen. Snoring. If anyone needs to hear that, say my name and I'll say it in their ear."His alibi. A handout, or her voice in the mayor's ear.
Why do we care?"A grateful consultant. Giants who owe us. A door into the deep roads no one else has." She looks away. "And a town of four thousand people. If that matters to you."Ironclad wants footholds.
Handout · custody log extract (give on request)
IRONCLAD INQUIRIES · CUSTODY DIVISION
ASSET: Gultor, Boon · bracelet sigil 19-K
LOCATION, night of the theft, 2nd–4th bell: Cell 19, Nexus sublevel 3
MOVEMENT: none · VITALS: asleep
attested, Turnkey Nine
Custody Log Extract
Loot · gear

Boon's alibi on Ironclad paper, stamped by Turnkey Nine. In Bagathorn it carries exactly as much weight as Ironclad's name, which is to say not much, until a giant agrees with it.

Soundtrack prompt · Cue · Through the Gate

An orchestral ambient soundtrack of three detectives stepping through a dimensional gate and landing in a cold dwarven mining town at night, performed by a full live symphony orchestra: a rising swirl of tremolo violins and harp glissandi, a sudden hush, then heavy low brass and timpani entering like a mountain clearing its throat, solo French horn over deep cellos and contrabassoon, a distant tubular bell. Wonder turning to dread. 66 BPM, C minor. Real acoustic instruments, concert-hall reverb, no synthesizers, no pads, no electronic sounds. Instrumental, no vocals.

The Gate

The Dimensional Gate sits in a round chamber at the bottom of a spiral stair, a ring of black iron taller than a house, its inner edge humming with a sound you feel in your fillings. A clerk checks a ledger, checks it again, and pulls a lever. The space inside the ring tears open like wet paper, and through it blows a wind that doesn't belong to the Nexus: cold, thin, smelling of coal smoke and frost and stone. Seraphine's voice, in your ear: "Dawn, Detectives. Don't make me come and get you." You step through. For one long heartbeat you are nowhere at all, falling sideways through grey. Then your boots hit stone, hard, and the cold closes over you like water.

You're standing in a town square halfway up a mountain, and the mountain is enormous. It fills the sky to the north, a black wall cutting out the stars, and Bagathorn clings to its shoulder in tiers: squat stone houses with turf roofs stacked terrace on terrace, stairways zigzagging between them, iron lift-cages hanging on chains between the levels like lanterns on a string. Every window is lit. Nobody in Bagathorn is asleep tonight.

Lantern Square is full. Dwarves in nightshirts and miners' coats, children wrapped in blankets on their parents' shoulders, a militia line in mismatched helmets clutching crossbows they don't know where to point. A cart of coal lies on its side where it tipped, its load spilled black across the granite. An old woman is filling buckets at the well for no reason anyone can see, because it gives her hands something to do. Somebody is ringing the bronze bell above it in short, nervous bursts, and somebody else is shouting at him to stop.

Then you notice the lanterns. Iron posts ring the square, a dozen of them, and every lantern is swinging. Not in the wind; there is no wind. They swing together, all the same way, slowly, like the pendulums of a dozen clocks keeping the same time. A crack runs across the flagstones under your feet. It looks new. It looks like it's still deciding where to go.

High above the town, at the very top of the slope, a red glow leaks from the mouth of the mine. And between you and it, on the highest tier, a slim black tower with a brass dome stands against the stars. Boon, you know that tower. You grew up in it.

The mountain moves

It starts under your feet, a vibration too low to hear, and then the whole mountain shrugs. The flagstones lift and settle like the deck of a ship. Dust pours off every roof in the square at once, a grey curtain in the lamplight. Somewhere a chimney goes, a long rumble and a crash, and the crowd moans, one voice, a sound like an animal in pain. The bell clangs on its own. Then it's over, and the lanterns go on swinging, and in the silence after it a child asks, very clearly, "Is it the giants, Mama?" And a voice near the well, an old miner's voice, answers for her: "No, love. That's the Bomber come home."

The crowd has seen Boon. Every face in Lantern Square turns.

The squareSocialDC 14 Persuasion · Intimidation · or Vali in Large Form (auto)

A wall of faces, a muttering that's getting louder, a militia line that has suddenly worked out where to point its crossbows. Somebody in the back picks up a lump of coal. What do you do?

Success

The muttering dies. Maybe it's the goliath who suddenly stands half again as tall as anyone in the square, or the steel in someone's voice, or the plain fact that three strangers just stepped out of thin air. The crowd gives ground, a step at a time, and a lane opens across the square. The man with the lump of coal looks at it as if he isn't sure how it got into his hand, and drops it.

Failure

The lump of coal sails out of the crowd and cracks against Boon's shoulder, and someone cheers, and someone else shouts "Olin Deepcut!" like a curse. It's ugly for a long moment, until a door bangs open across the square and a voice used to being obeyed says, "Enough." The crowd falls back. Not for you.

Cost: jot +1 on Bagathorn's Grudge. The militia will report where the party goes.

The client

He comes down the steps of the council hall leaning on a staff of black wood capped in brass, an old dwarf in a scholar's robe gone shiny at the elbows, his beard braided with the small copper beads of a man who has held a public office for forty years. He walks like his knees hurt and he will not let them show it. The crowd parts for him without being asked. He stops an arm's length from Boon and looks at him for a long time. His eyes are wet, and his face is perfectly still, as if the two have nothing to do with each other.

"Boon." Just the name. Then, to the other two, formally, with a short bow: "Bramm Gultor. I am the client. Thank you for coming." He doesn't offer to shake Boon's hand. His own, on the staff, is shaking. "You've come at a bad hour. They all are, now."

Bramm Gultor new
Boon's father · hereditary consultant to the mayor · the client · proud, stiff, lying by omission
Look
Old, upright by willpower; scholar's robe; copper beads of office in his beard; a black staff he leans on more than he admits
Voice
Formal, precise, a lecturer's cadence. Calls Boon "Boon" and never "son" until Scene 4.
Wants
The town saved. And the truth found, by someone who isn't him.
Hiding
He suspects Dorn. He will not say it aloud (DC 15 Insight: "He's afraid of what you'll find, and he wants you to find it anyway").

"I taught you everything I knew, Boon. It was the wrong everything."

Portrait prompt · Bramm Gultor (for an actor or token)

Painterly dark-fantasy character portrait, deep-mountain noir, cold blue-grey shadow cut by warm amber lamplight, drifting dust, highly detailed, 2:3 aspect ratio. An elderly dwarf scholar standing very straight in a town square at night, leaning on a black wooden staff capped with brass. Long iron-grey beard braided with small copper beads of office, heavy brows, wet eyes in a perfectly composed face. A worn midnight-blue scholar's robe gone shiny at the elbows, an inkstained cuff, a heavy brass key on a chain at his chest. Lantern light from one side, dust drifting down behind him. Proud, grieving, holding something back. No text, no watermark.

The mayor

A broad dwarf in a fur-collared coat over his nightshirt shoulders his way through the militia, chain of office bouncing on his chest, a face like a slammed door. Mayor Hesk Durrin looks at the three of you, then at Boon, and his lip actually curls. "So it's true. You spent the town's coin on him. " He rounds on Bramm. "The giants want the Gultor who broke the pact, Bramm. They said it plain, the one time they deigned to speak Common. Gultor. And look what walked out of the air." He jabs a finger at Boon's chest. "We've got till dawn. If your hired detectives haven't found me someone better by then, I'll give them this one, and I'll sleep fine."

Mayor Hesk Durrin new
Elected mayor of Bagathorn · Hostile to Boon
Wants
Someone to hand the giants before dawn, ideally someone nobody will miss
Hiding
He signed the order to dig the Ninth Gallery, on Dorn's survey, for the copper. He'd rather nobody looked at that too closely.
Turns
Backs down in public if Boon is cleared in front of witnesses. Seraphine's voice in his ear rattles him badly (he has never heard a voice come out of the air).

"I don't need the truth, detective. I need a name the giants will take."

If anyone says Seraphine's name: "Mayor Durrin. Mister Gultor was in my custody on the night in question, in a locked cell, asleep. I'd thank you not to waste my Detectives' time." Durrin goes white, looks around for the speaker, and stops jabbing.

The leads

Hand out the night's leads here. Let the players choose. Make sure these three surface:

  • Bramm: "The giants will speak only in their own tongue now, and we have no one who speaks it well enough to be understood. They sit at the Deepdelve's mouth and wait." Orek and Vali both speak Giant. → Scene 2.
  • A miner runs into the square, grey with dust, shouting for Bramm: "The Ninth's come down! The new shaft, the Gultor Shaft. Four men behind the fall, and Ragna's boy is one of them." → Scene 3.
  • Fennick, Boon's middle brother, catches Boon's sleeve as the crowd breaks up, too nervous to look at him: "Come to the tower. Not here. There's something I need to show you, and I can't say it with Father listening." → Scene 4.
Fennick Gultor new
Boon's middle brother · a minor wizard and the town's archivist · nervous, kind, loyal to everyone at once
Look
Ink on his fingers, spectacles pushed up into hair that won't lie flat, a coat buttoned wrong
Wants
His brothers not to destroy each other. Too late, on both counts.
Knows
Dorn's magic is failing. Dorn wears gloves now. Dorn went down the Gultor Shaft the night of the theft "to inspect the props." (Scene 4.)

"You look old, Boon. I mean that kindly. We all do."

Quick reference · Lantern Square
Look closerEvery lantern swings in time. The crack in the flagstones grows a finger's length while they talk. Families with bundles are already drifting toward the pass road.
HiddenDC 13 Perception on the council hall door, a notice in Durrin's hand: "By order: the Ninth Gallery shall be opened toward the copper seam, per the survey of D. Gultor." (A first clue toward Dorn.)
SensesLanterns creaking in time · the nervous bell · coal smoke, frost, wet stone · breath-fog · the faint, constant tremble underfoot, like standing on a sleeping animal
Who's hereBramm Gultor, Mayor Durrin, Fennick Gultor: see their cards.Gilda Two-Pails: the old woman at the well. Knew Boon as a boy; gives him a cup of water without a word, the only kindness in the square.Sergeant Orsk: militia, sixty, would rather be in bed; follows the party if the square went badly.
Rumors"The giants are here to eat us" (false) · "The new shaft dug into a giant's grave" (close: a giant's bed) · "The Gultors made a deal with the giants, long ago" (true) · "The Bomber came back to finish the job" (false)
On returnAfter clock 4: half the square has fled up the pass road; the militia has orders to find Boon.

Ask the table

  • Boon, what's the first thing you recognize, and does it make you feel better or worse?
  • Orek, what did you tell Seraphine to call you?
  • Vali, there are children in that square. What do you do with your hands?

If the party…

Asks Bramm what was stolen"I don't know." (True.) "I know what it's for." (He won't say more in public. Scene 4.)
Asks Bramm about the pact"Old business. Ask the giants. They remember it better than we do."
Splits upFine. Run scenes in parallel and tick the clock once for both.
Clues: "the Gultor who broke the pact"; Boon's alibi; Dorn's name on the survey order (if found)Clock: +1 as they leave the square
Leads to · Scene 2 · 3 · 43 paths
Up the Ore RoadGo to Scene 2 →

NudgeBramm: "They will not speak to us in Common again. You have their tongue, both of you. Please." He gives them his staff's brass cap to show the giants: the Gultor seal. Sergeant Orsk walks them as far as the last houses.

The Ore Road leaves the top of the town in a long switchback, broad enough for two carts, its stones polished by a hundred years of iron wheels. You climb past the last houses, where faces watch you from behind shutters, past the slag heaps steaming faintly in the cold, past a mule standing alone in the road with its harness cut, waiting for someone who isn't coming back for it. The higher you go, the quieter it gets. The town's noise falls away beneath you. No picks ring out. No carts rattle. You climb the last switchback, and the road ahead goes still.

Then read the Scene 2 arrival.

To the Gultor ShaftGo to Scene 3 →

NudgeThe grey-faced miner, already running back the way he came: "Four men! Tam Deepcut's one! Ragna's at the shaft head, she won't leave it." Boon knows the name Deepcut. Olin Deepcut died in his explosion.

The miner runs, and you run after him: up a stairway cut into the rock behind the council hall, through a lift-cage that groans on its chain as it hauls you up a tier, out across a goat path above the rooftops where Bagathorn's chimneys smoke beneath your boots. The town drops away. The path turns to loose scree that slides and chatters under your feet, and the cold bites harder up here, out of the shelter of the houses. The miner doesn't slow down. He's praying under his breath, the same three words over and over. The path tops a rise of loose stone, and ahead of you, in the dark, a big wheel is creaking as it turns.

Then read the Scene 3 arrival.

Up the Consul's StairGo to Scene 4 →

NudgeFennick, already walking away: "The tower. The study door will be open. Father's staying at the council hall all night. Dorn's with him." A beat. "Mostly."

The Consul's Stair climbs straight up through the town, three hundred steps cut into the living rock, worn into shallow bowls by four centuries of Gultors going up and down to give advice. Boon, your feet remember every one. Halfway up there's a step with a crack shaped like a lightning bolt, and you stepped over it every day of your childhood because your brothers said it was bad luck, and you step over it now before you can stop yourself. Doors close as you pass. A shutter bangs. Above you the town thins out, the houses grow older and grander and quieter, and you climb the last flight.

Then read the Scene 4 arrival.

2

The Court at the Mine Mouth

Late nightThe Deepdelve pithead
Who: Thrunna Stonesinger, Kolgrim, Old Hagga, Corporal Nella Brask and the barricade militiaLeans on: Vali Orek Boon
Why they're here
  • Bramm asked: the giants speak only Giant now, and Orek and Vali both do (Scene 1).
  • Seraphine's case card: "Do not speak first." Nobody yet knows what was stolen. The giants do.

The scene's job: learn what was taken and what dawn means; clear Boon (by smell); keep Kolgrim from starting early (talk him down, or beat him in the optional duel); earn the Stone-Lullaby and the rune-token. Clock +1 when the scene ends.

Art prompt · The Deepdelve pithead

Painterly dark-fantasy concept art, deep-mountain noir, cold blue-grey granite and soot-black shadow cut by warm amber lantern light, veins of pale opalescent violet glowing in the stone, drifting rock dust in the air, cinematic composition, highly detailed environment, 16:9 aspect ratio. A broad apron of black stone cut into the flank of a huge mountain at night, the dark mouth of an old dwarven mine at its back, flanked by colossal carved door-pillars worn almost smooth. Rusted rail lines run out of the tunnel and stop. A towering timber winding-gear and a row of ore carts overturned into a crude barricade, crossbows resting on them. In the middle of the apron, an ore cart full of burning coal glows like a brazier, and around it sit three enormous grey boulders that might be people: one shaped like a hunched figure with moss on its shoulders, one tall and still, one half-risen. Fresh rune-carvings glow faintly violet on the rock face behind them. Stars above, a red glow from the tunnel mouth, dust hanging in the firelight. Ancient, solemn, about to break. No people, no text, no watermark.

Soundtrack prompt · The Court at the Mine Mouth

An orchestral ambient soundtrack of three ancient stone giants holding court at a mine mouth in the middle of the night, performed by a full live symphony orchestra kept very quiet: sustained low cellos and double basses holding one deep note, a slow contrabassoon and tuba line like something huge breathing, soft timpani rolls like distant rockfall, a solemn French horn chorale, and a lone alto flute carrying an old, simple lullaby melody above it all. Vast, patient, grave. 48 BPM, A Aeolian. Real acoustic instruments, concert-hall reverb, no synthesizers, no pads, no electronic sounds. Loopable, instrumental, no vocals.

The pithead of the Deepdelve is a broad apron of black stone cut into the mountain's flank, big enough to turn a wagon team, and the mine's mouth gapes at the back of it, framed by two colossal pillars so old their carvings have worn down to suggestions: a hand, an eye, something that might once have been a face. Rail lines run out of the dark and simply stop. The winding-gear stands idle against the stars, its great wheel still.

Somebody has tipped half a dozen ore carts on their sides across the road to make a barricade, and behind it crouch a dozen dwarves of the town militia, crossbows propped on the iron rims, their breath smoking. None of them has fired. None of them, you suspect, has blinked in an hour. A young corporal with a bandaged ear lifts her head as you come up and whispers, as if the night might overhear her, "Don't go past the carts. Please. They don't like it when you go past the carts."

In the middle of the apron, someone has lit a fire in an ore cart. Coal glows in it, red and steady, and around it sit three boulders. That's what you think at first: three grey boulders, each the size of a cottage. Then one of them moves. It turns its head, and grit sifts from its shoulders like sand from a dune, and you see a face carved by centuries rather than hands, grey and creased and calm, with eyes like two pale river stones. Its fingertip is resting against the mountain's face, and as it moves it leaves behind a line of rune-carving that glows, faintly, violet.

The second boulder is taller and hasn't moved at all, and moss grows thick on its shoulders. The third is half-risen, one knee planted, fists on the ground, and when it sees you it bares a row of teeth like gravestones. The ground under your feet is humming. Very faintly, from somewhere deep beneath the mountain, so low you feel it rather than hear it, something is breathing.

Do not speak first

Stone giants hold that the speaker who opens a conversation owns its end. Seraphine's card warned them. If a PC speaks first, Thrunna doesn't answer; she lets the silence run until they stop (and this scene's checks are at disadvantage until someone apologizes in Giant). If they wait, or kneel, or show Bramm's brass Gultor seal, she speaks.

The giant at the rock face lifts her fingertip from the stone. When she speaks, her voice doesn't come from her mouth so much as from everywhere at once, from the rock under your boots and the cart full of coal and the iron rims of the barricade, which buzz faintly, so the militia flinch and grip their crossbows. She speaks in Giant, slowly, each word set down like a stone in a wall.

"Small ones come up the road again. These ones have waited. That is better manners than the one with the chain on his chest." The river-stone eyes move from face to face and stop, with mild interest, on Vali. She tilts her great head. "Oh. And a cousin. A dreaming cousin, walking in the dream, wearing it like a cloak." Something like a smile moves through the creases of her face, the way a crack moves through ice. "Sit, cousin. Sit by the fire. You are the first of our blood to come to the Bed in four hundred years."

Thrunna Stonesinger new
Stone giant · speaker for the folk of Dhurak-Ul · grave, patient, absolute · Neutral → Friendly to Vali
Look
Grey and creased as a cliff face; pale river-stone eyes; rune-carving with a fingertip as she talks
Voice
Slow; each word set down like a stone. Calls the surface "the dream," dwarves "small ones," goliaths "cousins."
Believes
The world above the stone is a dream; deeds done in it are not real. That is why giants don't come up: they would do terrible things, and not care.
Wants
The Eye in Ammaskar's hand before dawn, and the thief given to the mountain
Stats
Stone Giant (SRD) if it ever comes to that. It shouldn't.

"In the dream there are no debts. That is why we do not come up. But the thief carried a waking thing into the dream, and that is real."

Portrait prompt · Thrunna Stonesinger (for an actor or token)

Painterly dark-fantasy character portrait, deep-mountain noir, cold blue-grey shadow cut by warm amber firelight, drifting rock dust, highly detailed, 2:3 aspect ratio. An ancient female stone giant seated by a fire of coal in an iron ore cart, her skin grey and deeply creased like weathered granite, with faint veins of pale violet crystal running under it. Her eyes are smooth pale river stones, calm and unreadable. Long grey hair bound in thick ropes with rings of carved slate. One huge fingertip rests against a rock face, leaving a glowing line of violet runes. A cloak of stitched mountain-goat hides over her shoulders, grit sifting down from it. Solemn, patient, immeasurably old. No text, no watermark.

What was taken

Thrunna looks past you, down at the town glittering on the slope below, as if it were a reflection in water. "Under this mountain, far down, where the stone is warm, lies Ammaskar. Our grandmother's grandmother. She lay down to sleep before your kind had learned to cut a window, and she sleeps still, and while she sleeps, she dreams, and her dreaming holds the Bed still." She lays her palm flat on the apron, and the humming in the stone steadies under it for a moment, like a frightened animal under a hand. "She dreams through a stone. We call it her Eye. It sat in her open hand for nine hundred years."

"Two nights ago a small one walked through our wards with no heartbeat and no footfall, and blew a hole in the wall of her hall, and took the Eye out of her hand." The river-stone eyes come back to you. "It wept when it did it. We heard the weeping. We heard nothing else."

"Without the Eye, she wakes. A little every hour. You feel her breathing now. At dawn she will open her eyes, and sit up, as anyone does when they wake." She looks down at Bagathorn, tier on tier on the mountain's shoulder, every window lit. "Your town is built upon her chest."

Soundtrack prompt · Cue · The giants rise

An orchestral ambient soundtrack of three stone giants rising to their full height at a mine mouth to deliver an ultimatum, performed by a full live symphony orchestra: a slow, enormous crescendo from silence, double basses and contrabassoon climbing, timpani and bass drum rolls like a landslide gathering, a massive trombone and tuba chorale stating a stern, ancient theme, cymbal swell to a towering peak, then a sudden cut to a single sustained low cello note. Overwhelming, solemn, final. 54 BPM, F minor. Real acoustic instruments, concert-hall reverb, no synthesizers, no pads, no electronic sounds. Instrumental, no vocals.

The terms

All three giants stand. It takes a long time. Stone grinds on stone; grit pours from their shoulders in rivers; the militia behind the barricade scramble backward, one of them sobbing. The moss-shouldered one rises last, and it is the largest thing you have ever seen move. They stand against the stars like the mountain's own sentries, and the fire in the ore cart looks like a candle at their feet.

"Before the sun," says Thrunna, and the whole mountainside says it with her, "the Eye goes back into her hand. And the Gultor who broke the pact is given to us, and we will give him to the mountain, and he will lie in the stone and dream until he understands what he did. A hundred years. Perhaps less, if he is quick." A pause. "If not, we go back down to our grandmother's side, and sing to her, and when she sits up we will be glad of it, because we will see her face again."

Hear the giantsSocial · in GiantDC 15 Persuasion or HistoryVali: advantage (kin)Orek: speaks Giant

Only those who speak Giant can address Thrunna directly; anyone else speaks through a translator at disadvantage. What do you ask of her, and what do you offer?

Success

Thrunna lowers herself back down by the fire, which is how you know you've been heard. "You speak like small ones who have listened before." She tells you everything: the pact Haldra Gultor made, three hundred years gone, that no dwarf would dig below the Eighth Gallery and that a Gultor would always keep it; that the Hush only opens giant wards if its bearer speaks the pact-word, which only Haldra's line was ever given; and, because you asked well, she offers to teach one of you the song her people sing to Ammaskar when she stirs.

Unlocks the Stone-Lullaby (below) and the full Q&A.

Failure

Thrunna listens to the end, and then turns back to the rock face and resumes carving, which is an answer. Kolgrim laughs, a sound like a cart of gravel being emptied. She gives you the terms again, word for word, and nothing more, and the hour slides by while you try to find another way in.

Cost: clock +1. No lullaby yet (it can still be found in Haldra's papers in Scene 4). The pact-word clue must come from Bramm.

"Which of you is Gultor?" Boon

Corporal Brask's voice cracks across the apron from behind the carts, high and desperate: "That one! He's a Gultor! The Mayor says take that one!" Every crossbow on the barricade swings toward Boon.

Thrunna doesn't look at the corporal. She looks at Boon. Then she leans down, and down, until her face is level with yours and so close you can see the grit in the creases of her skin and feel the cold that comes off her like the cold off a cave mouth. She breathes in, long and slow, through a nose like a cleft in a cliff. Your hair stirs toward her.

She straightens. "Black powder," she says. "Iron. Old sorrow, very deep, like water in a well." A pause. "No ink. The thief smelled of the ink Gultors use to sign the pact, blue-black, with stone in it. This one has not touched that ink in many years." She turns her great head toward the barricade, and every crossbow there drops at once. "Tell your chief with the chain: we know the smell of the one we want. Do not bring us the wrong small one. We would know. And we would be angry."

That clears Boon of the theft in front of a dozen witnesses. Word reaches the square within the hour: Mayor Durrin no longer has a case, only a grudge.

Kolgrim

The half-risen giant hasn't sat back down. Kolgrim is younger than the others, if anything carved from a mountain can be young, and angry the way young things are angry, with his whole body. He takes one step forward, and the apron cracks under his heel. "Talk, talk, talk. Why wait for the sun?" He looks at the barricade the way you'd look at a line of ants. "Sing her awake now. Let her sit up. Let the dream fall off her like dust. They are only small ones, Thrunna. They are not even real."

Face down KolgrimSocial or a show of strengthDC 16 Intimidation · or Persuasion through ThrunnaVali: advantage in Large Form

A giant three times your height is deciding whether you're real. What do you do?

Success

Kolgrim stops. Maybe it's the goliath who grew to stand eye-to-belt with him, or the quiet certainty in someone's voice, or Thrunna's hand landing on his arm like a lid on a pot. He looks down at you for a long time, nostrils flaring. Then he grunts, and sits, heavily, and the whole mountainside shivers with it. "Dawn," he says. "Not one breath after." Thrunna: "He will wait. I will make him."

Cancels the clock-7 effect: Kolgrim won't start singing early.

Failure

Kolgrim snorts, and kicks the nearest ore cart off the barricade. It flies end over end across the apron, scattering dwarves like birds, and smashes into the winding-gear. Thrunna says one word, sharp as a hammer on a chisel, and he stops. But he doesn't sit. He stands at the edge of the firelight, fists clenched, and begins, very softly, to hum.

Cost: whoever is nearest makes a DC 16 Dex save against the flying cart, 4d10 bludgeoning, half on a success (Vali's Interpose Shield works). The clock-7 effect stays live.

Optional fight · Kolgrim's Test8,300 XP · Low–ModerateRun this instead of the check above if the table wants a brawl: a ritual duel inside a ring, with rules, a yield point and a payoff at the climax.

Thrunna doesn't scold him. She looks at Kolgrim the way a grandmother looks at a boy who has said something stupid at the table, and then she looks at you, and something like amusement moves through the creases of her face. "He thinks you are not real. That is what the young believe about the dream." She settles back by the fire. "Teach him."

Kolgrim grins. It's a terrible grin, all gravestone teeth. He drags one heel through the apron in a wide circle around the fire, and the black stone peels up behind it like soil behind a plough, a ring sixty feet across. Then he slaps both palms flat on the ground and sings one harsh note, and the apron answers: three shapes heave up out of the rock around the ring, blunt and grey and featureless, stone servants pulled out of the mountain like loaves from an oven. Kolgrim pulls a boulder the size of a cart off the slag heap and hefts it onto his shoulder. "Hit me, small ones. If you are real, I will feel it. If I feel it, I will believe you." He laughs, and the whole mountainside laughs with him. "The first to kneel loses."

Battle map prompt · The Deepdelve pithead (30 × 24 squares)

Top-down orthographic fantasy battle map for a virtual tabletop, hand-painted digital illustration, lush and intricately detailed, saturated jewel-tone palette with deep contrasting shadows, dramatic glowing light sources casting colored pools of light, rich textures on stone, timber, moss and water, crisp readable shapes that stay clear under tokens, flat overhead view with no perspective tilt, medieval fantasy setting. A landscape map of a broad black-stone apron cut into a mountainside at night, laid out for a 30 by 24 square grid. Along the north edge, the dark mouth of an old mine framed by two colossal round stone pillar bases, with iron rail tracks running out of it and ending abruptly mid-apron, one rusted ore cart still on the rails. At the center, an iron ore cart heaped with glowing orange coal acts as a brazier, ringed by a freshly gouged circular furrow in the stone about twelve squares across. Three giant-sized boulders sit around the fire like seats. A tall timber winding-gear with a huge spoked wheel stands to the east beside steaming grey slag heaps. A line of overturned ore carts forms a barricade along the south edge where a cart road leaves the map. The west edge is a sheer cliff drop with a broken wooden railing. Faint glowing violet veins run through cracks in the stone. No people, no creatures, no text, letters, numbers or symbols, no grid lines, no modern objects.

Soundtrack prompt · Combat loop · Kolgrim's Test

An orchestral ambient soundtrack of a ritual duel against a young stone giant inside a ring of firelight at a mine mouth, performed by a full live symphony orchestra: enormous slow bass drum and timpani hits like giant footsteps, a stomping tuba and contrabassoon ostinato, bold French horn fanfares answering each blow, sweeping string runs between strikes, ringing anvil accents, a proud trumpet theme growing braver as the fight turns. Mighty, rough, exhilarating. 104 BPM, D minor. Real acoustic instruments, concert-hall reverb, no synthesizers, no pads, no electronic sounds. Loopable, instrumental, no vocals.

Encounter · Kolgrim's TestStone Giant + 3 Earth Elementals (SRD)8,300 XP
Foes
Kolgrim: Stone Giant (SRD) with 200 HP; add a Rock Catching reaction. Stone servants ×3: Earth Elemental (SRD), crumbling to gravel when Kolgrim yields.
The rules
A ritual, not a murder. Kolgrim yields at 100 HP, sits down hard, and the servants collapse. A PC dropped to 0 is stable, and Kolgrim roars with laughter. If the party yields, or two of them are down, the test is lost. Thrunna and Old Hagga don't join in.
Tactics
Kolgrim opens by throwing his boulder (Rock, 4d10+6) at whoever looks smallest, then wades in with Greatclub. The servants try to shove PCs out of the ring and into the fire. He targets Vali in Large Form last; that's the one he wants to beat properly.
Terrain
  • The ring: a creature shoved out of the furrow can't attack Kolgrim until it steps back in (Thrunna's rule).
  • The coal-cart fire: a creature shoved into it takes 2d6 fire and catches alight (1d6 per turn until an action puts it out).
  • The rail cart: an action and DC 14 Athletics sends it rolling down the tracks: 4d6 bludgeoning in a 20-ft line, DC 14 Dex for half.
  • Giant-seat boulders: three-quarters cover for Medium creatures; Kolgrim can pick one up to throw (bonus action).
  • The winding wheel: knock out its brake pin (DC 15 Sleight of Hand or tools) and the cable whips loose across the ring: DC 15 Dex save, 3d8 slashing to everything in a 30-ft line.
  • The cliff edge (west): a creature shoved off falls 30 ft onto scree (3d6) and is out of the ring.
Spotlight
Vali Large Form eye-to-belt with a giant, Vow of Enmity, smites · Orek Trip Attack to put a giant on his back · Boon force-ballista cannon from behind a boulder, and the winding wheel
The end of the testNo rollWon or lost
Won

Kolgrim goes down on one knee. The whole apron jumps. He kneels there for a long moment, breathing like a forge bellows, grit streaming from a crack across his chest. Then he starts to laugh: huge, delighted, helpless laughter that shakes dust off the pillars. "Real," he says. "Very real. Ow." He looks at you with his gravestone grin, and it isn't terrible anymore. "Dawn. Not one breath before. I promise it on the stone." Thrunna, by the fire, doesn't look up from her carving. "Good," she says. "He needed that."

Cancels the clock-7 effect: Kolgrim won't start singing early. He'll fight beside the party in Scene 5 if they ask: one free Greatclub attack per round on Dorn.

Lost

Kolgrim stands over you, not even breathing hard, and pats the top of someone's head with one enormous finger, almost kindly. "Not real," he decides. "Pretty, though. Like dreams are." He walks back to the edge of the firelight, sits, and begins, very softly, to hum. The stone under your feet hums with him.

Cost: the clock-7 effect stays live.

The Stone-Lullaby if earned

Thrunna takes whoever offers, cousin or small one, and sets one enormous fingertip, very gently, on their breastbone, the way you'd hold a bird. Then she sings. It isn't loud. It's so low it seems to come up out of the mountain into your chest, and settle there, and stay. Four lines, over and over, until you find you're singing it too, without having decided to. Out in the dark beyond the firelight, for as long as the song lasts, the breathing under the mountain slows.

Handout · the Stone-Lullaby (Giant, with Thrunna's meaning)
Dhura, dhura, Ammaskar,
ost hallun, ost vellar,
helm a'Oghu, helm a'nar,
sove: Dhurak-Ul vaer.

Hush, hush, Ammaskar,
stone lies down, stone lies far.
Hold the Eye, and hold the dark.
Sleep: the mountain is your bed.

Whoever learns it auto-succeeds on the "Sing her down" step in Scene 5.

Thrunna's gift Vali

Before you go, Thrunna presses something into Vali's palm: a disc of grey slate the size of a coin, warm as a hearthstone, carved on one face with a single rune that glows faintly violet. "For the cousin. Our wards will know you, and our guardians will let you pass. If you find the thief below, hold it up, and they will remember who they are guarding."

Stonesinger's Rune-Token
Consumable · trinket · uncommon (5 charges)

Giant wards and the Sleeper's dream-guardians treat the bearer as kin and won't attack them. Spend a charge to cast meld into stone. Held up in Ammaskar's hall, the guardians turn on the thief instead (Scene 5).

Thrunna's answers · for the questions players will ask
They askThrunna saysDM truth
What does the Eye look like?"A stone as big as your fist, dark as the bottom of a well. Lights move in it, slow, like fish under ice. Those are her dreams."A violet-black geode. It hums near Orek.
What does it do?"It drinks from whoever holds it. It finds the river of magic in them and drinks, and pours her dream back in. Small ones who hold it can do great things. For a while."Lets the holder cast through it; turns them to stone. A body with no river can't be drunk from (it's inert for Boon).
Why not find the thief yourselves?"We do not walk into the dream. In the dream nothing is real, so nothing matters. We would step on your houses and not notice. That is why the pact."A threat they don't mean as one.
What was the pact?"Haldra Gultor came down with a lamp and no fear. She said: we will dig no deeper than the eighth hall, and one of my blood will always keep that promise. We said: then the Bed will be still. It was still, three hundred years."The Gultor consultancy began as the pact-keeper's office.
How did the thief pass your wards?"Our wards listen for hearts and feet. It had neither. And it spoke the pact-word at the door, the word we gave Haldra's line and no other."A Hush charm from the Nexus Bazaar, plus the pact-word: a Gultor.
What will you do to the thief?"Give him to the stone. He will lie in it and dream. When he wakes he will be wiser, or he will be stone. That is not cruelty, cousin. It is time."A hundred years sealed in rock.
Can she be put back to sleep?"Put the Eye back in her hand, the way it sat. Sing to her. If you are quick, and she has not fully opened her eyes, she will sigh, and turn over, and dream again."The four steps in Scene 5.
Quick reference · the Deepdelve pithead
Look closerThe rune-carving on the rock face is a record: Thrunna is writing down tonight as it happens. The tunnel mouth breathes warm air that smells of hot stone. Vali, with Divine Sense: the whole mountain beneath you reads faintly consecrated, like an altar the size of a range.
HiddenDC 14 History or Arcana the worn carvings on the door-pillars show a dwarf with a lamp facing a sleeping giant across a line: the pact, carved three hundred years ago. A tiny Gultor seal is cut into the dwarf's lamp.
SensesFirelight on grey stone · a hum underfoot; a slow breath under the mountain · hot coal and cold rock · the giants' cold, like a cave mouth · the taste of grit
Who's hereKolgrim: young, furious, wants it over. Sits if faced down.Old Hagga: the moss-shouldered one; never speaks; opens one eye if anyone sings the lullaby, and closes it again, satisfied.Corporal Nella Brask: militia, bandaged ear (Kolgrim's first warning shout burst her eardrum), terrified, honest.
RumorsFrom the militia: "The new shaft was the Gultor boy's idea. Dorn's. For the copper." (true) · "Ragna Deepcut's lad is down the Ninth." (true)
On returnAfter clock 6: the fire is out and the giants are gone, down into the mine. Only Old Hagga remains, sitting, eyes closed, humming the lullaby to the mountain.
Stat noteThrunna, Kolgrim, Old Hagga: Stone Giant (SRD). Kolgrim's optional test is the only fight here; Thrunna and Hagga never join a fight.

Ask the table

  • Vali, the giants call you cousin. Does it feel like a kindness or a claim?
  • Orek, the giants speak of the Eye the way your father spoke of his best stones. What do you feel?
  • Boon, a giant just told a dozen militia you're innocent. What's on your face?

If the party…

Offers Boon as the GultorThrunna smells him and refuses. "Do not insult me twice."
Asks to see Ammaskar"Bring the Eye, and the cousin may come down with it." (They'll see her in Scene 5 either way.)
Attacks Thrunna or HaggaThrunna stops singing the mountain still. Clock +2. The test is one thing; this is another.
Clues: the thief is a Gultor (ink, pact-word); Boon is innocent (smell); the Eye drinks from the holder's magic; how to put her backClock: +1 as they leave (+1 more on a failed hearing)Result: Kolgrim faced down (or his test won or lost)
Leads to · Scene 3 · 4 · 53 paths
Across the mountainsideGo to Scene 3 →

NudgeThrunna: "The hole in her wall is at the end of your newest tunnel. Your small ones are trapped in it; we hear their hearts. Four. Quick, and frightened." Corporal Brask points the way across the slope to the new headframe.

A miners' track leaves the pithead and runs sideways across the face of the mountain, a ledge no wider than a cart, with the town's lights a long way down on your left and black rock on your right. You go single file. The giants' fire shrinks behind you to a red coal and then to nothing. Twice the ledge shudders under your boots and you press yourselves flat to the rock until it stops, and pebbles go skittering off the edge into the dark, and you never hear them land. Then the ledge widens into a slope of loose scree, and you climb it, and at the top, where the scree gives way to trampled mud, you hear voices ahead: low, worn, a crowd that has been waiting a long time.

Then read the Scene 3 arrival.

Down to the towerGo to Scene 4 →

NudgeThe thief is a Gultor. Thrunna, as they turn to go: "Ask the old one with the staff what his family did with Haldra's word. Someone kept it badly." Boon knows who the Gultors are. There are four of them left.

You go down the Ore Road at a pace just short of running, and Bagathorn comes up to meet you, tier by tier, every window lit, every street full of people carrying things: a clock, a cradle, a cage with a songbird in it. Nobody looks at you now. Word has run ahead of you down the mountain, and the faces that turned toward Boon in hate an hour ago turn away from him now, uncertain. At the top of the town you leave the road for the Consul's Stair, and the noise drops away below you, and you climb the last flight.

Then read the Scene 4 arrival.

The giants' roadGo to Scene 5 →

NudgeOnly at clock 6, if the party is still at the pithead (or returns to it). Thrunna's head snaps toward the tunnel: "The thief has gone back to her. He is in the hall. Cousin, come." She opens a road through the rock that no dwarf has ever walked.

Thrunna walks into the mine mouth, lays her palm on the back wall of the tunnel, and sings one long, low note. The rock opens. Not with a crack or a rumble; it parts, slow and soft as a curtain, and beyond it a stair goes down, each step as tall as your waist, worn into a shallow bowl by giant feet. You climb down it in the light of your lamps, the giants ahead of you filling the passage like moving walls. It goes down a very long way. The air gets warmer, and thicker, and the breathing under the mountain gets louder, until it isn't under you anymore, it's around you. Ahead, through a split in the rock, there's a glow the color of a bruise.

Then read the Scene 5 arrival.
