The Ninth Gallery

Small hoursThe Gultor Shaft → the Ninth Gallery
Who: Ragna Deepcut, Foreman Brokk Harl, Tam Deepcut and three trapped miners, two dream-guardiansLeans on: Boon Vali Orek
Why they're here
  • Four miners are trapped behind a fall in the Ninth Gallery, and Ragna Deepcut's son is one of them (Scene 1).
  • Thrunna: the hole in Ammaskar's wall is at the end of the newest tunnel (Scene 2).

The scene's job: the big action set piece. Get the miners out while starving xorns come through the walls, then read the breach like a crime scene, with the dream-guardians as a second wave. Boon meets his own bomb. Clock +2 when the scene ends (the descent and the dig take time).

Art prompt · The Gultor Shaft headframe

Painterly dark-fantasy concept art, deep-mountain noir, cold blue-grey granite and soot-black shadow cut by warm amber lantern light, veins of pale opalescent violet glowing in the stone, drifting rock dust in the air, cinematic composition, highly detailed environment, 16:9 aspect ratio. A brand-new mine headframe of raw pale timber high on a dark mountainside at night, sap still beading on the beams, its great iron winding wheel turning slowly above a black square shaft. Beside it a small stone lamp shed with its door open, warm light spilling out over rows of brass miners' lamps hanging on numbered pegs, several pegs empty. A rough plank foreman's shack with papers nailed to its wall and a red-painted powder locker. A crowd of shawled shapes waiting in the cold by the shaft mouth, abandoned picks and a cart in the mud, steam rising from the shaft. Far below, the lights of a terraced town. Bitter cold, breath-fog, anxious vigil. No people, no text, no watermark.

Art prompt · The Ninth Gallery & the breach

Painterly dark-fantasy concept art, deep-mountain noir, cold blue-grey granite and soot-black shadow cut by warm amber lantern light, veins of pale opalescent violet glowing in the stone, drifting rock dust in the air, cinematic composition, highly detailed environment, 16:9 aspect ratio. A long, low, freshly cut mine tunnel deep underground, lit by a few hanging brass lamps, timber props groaning under the weight of the ceiling, rail tracks underfoot running through ankle-deep black water. Midway along, a fresh rockfall half blocks the tunnel. At the far end, the rough dwarven tunnel stops dead against ancient, enormous, perfectly smooth worked stone, where a ragged hole has been blasted through, scorched in a star pattern; the hole is now plugged by a bulging wall of new grey stone, smooth as poured wax, laced with glowing veins of pale violet crystal that pulse slowly like breathing. Splinters of brass and wire on the floor, a single small dark crystal glinting in the water. Claustrophobic, tense, uncanny. No people, no text, no watermark.

Soundtrack prompt · The Ninth Gallery

An orchestral ambient soundtrack of a desperate rescue deep in a collapsing mine, performed by a small live orchestra: a relentless low pulse of col legno strings and soft timpani like dripping water and distant hammering, sul ponticello violas creaking like timber props, a muted horn calling and getting no answer, sudden swells of tremolo cellos for each tremor, and a fragile solo oboe line of hope that keeps breaking off. Claustrophobic, urgent, human. 96 BPM, E Phrygian. Real acoustic instruments, concert-hall reverb, no synthesizers, no pads, no electronic sounds. Loopable, instrumental, no vocals.

The Gultor Shaft is so new the timber still bleeds. Its headframe stands against the stars on a shelf of raw rock high above the town, a tower of pale, freshly cut beams with sap beading along the joints and glittering in the lamplight like sweat. The great iron wheel at its top turns slowly, groaning, paying out cable into a square black hole in the mountain, and from that hole comes a breath of warm air that steams in the cold.

Around the shaft mouth, perhaps thirty people stand in the mud, wrapped in shawls and blankets and coats thrown on over nightclothes. They aren't talking. They've been here long enough that there's nothing left to say. A boy of ten is holding a miner's lamp that isn't lit, as if it belonged to someone. Off to one side, a plank shack has papers nailed all over its wall, and a red-painted locker beside it is chained shut with a sign that says POWDER in letters a foot high.

The light comes from a small stone shed by the headframe, its door wide open: the lamp room. Inside, brass miners' lamps hang on numbered pegs in long, neat rows. Four of the pegs are empty. A woman stands in the doorway with her arms folded, a broad, grey-haired dwarf in a leather apron with soot ground permanently into the creases of her hands. She is the only one here who isn't looking at the shaft. She is looking at you. At Boon. And her face, which was worried, goes very still and very hard.

The lamp-warden Boon

Ragna Deepcut walks out of the lamp room, through the mud, across the space the crowd clears for her, and stops in front of Boon. She is shorter than you remember. Everyone is. She looks at your face for a long time, and at the bracelet on your wrist, and then she spits on the ground at your feet, carefully, not on your boots, the way you'd do a thing you'd been planning for thirty years.

"Olin's peg was number twelve," she says. Her voice is very quiet. "I've kept it empty. Thirty-one years." She tips her head at the lamp room without looking away from you. "My boy's peg is thirty. That one's empty too, tonight. He's down there behind a fall in a tunnel your brother told them to dig." She draws a breath. "So here's what's going to happen, Gultor. You're going to go down there, and you're going to bring my Tam up. And if you're going to kill another Deepcut tonight, you'll start with me, and you'll do it up here where I can see you coming."

She turns and walks back into the lamp room, and comes out with lamps, and hands one each to the others. She doesn't hand one to Boon. She hangs his on a peg by the door and leaves it there for him to take himself.

Ragna Deepcut new
Lamp-warden of the Deepdelve · widow of Olin Deepcut, killed in Boon's explosion · Hostile to Boon
Look
Broad, grey, leather apron, soot ground into her knuckles; keeps peg twelve empty
Wants
Tam up alive. Then, if there's any justice, never to see Boon again.
Turns
If Tam comes up alive and she later reads Dorn's journal: she gives Boon Olin's lamp at dawn.

"I don't need you sorry. I need you careful."

Foreman Brokk "Two-Thumbs" Harl new
Foreman of the Gultor Shaft · Friendly to anyone who'll get his crew out
Knows
The Ninth was dug "on Master Dorn's survey, straight as a die, toward a copper seam we never found." Dorn came down alone two nights ago, late, "to inspect the props."
Gives
The powder-locker key and three blasting charges, if anyone asks, and the copy of the survey charter off the shack wall.

"Never found a lick of copper. Just kept going, because the paper said to."

Handout · nailed to the foreman's shack
BY ORDER OF THE MAYOR OF BAGATHORN
The NINTH GALLERY shall be cut from the new shaft
at a bearing of north-north-east, level, two hundred yards,
toward a seam of copper indicated by survey.
Survey and bearing certified by D. Gultor, Consultant's Office.
Note: Pact limit (8th Gallery) does not apply; new shaft, new count. — D.G.

DC 12 Investigation or History: Dorn started the gallery count over at the new shaft to get around the pact. The "Ninth" is deeper than anything Haldra allowed.

Deepdelve Blasting Charge
Consumable · trinket · ×3 · from the powder locker

Action to set, 1-minute fuse or a spark. 4d6 fire + bludgeoning (half each) in a 15-ft radius, DC 13 Dex for half. Double damage to objects and structures. In Boon's hands, with tinker's tools, the radius can be shaped down to a 5-ft cone.

The Long Drop

The cage is a box of iron bars on a cable, big enough for six dwarves or one goliath and two of anybody. Brokk bangs the bell twice, the wheel groans overhead, and the floor falls out from under your stomach. The shaft walls slide upward past the bars, raw and wet and gleaming in your lamplight, banded with seams of grey and black and, here and there, a vein of something that glitters violet and is gone. The warm air rushes up past you, smelling of wet stone and lamp oil and, faintly, of something sweet, like the inside of a church. Down, and down, and down. The circle of stars above you shrinks to a coin, to a point, to nothing. Then the cage jolts to a stop, swaying, at the mouth of a tunnel, and somewhere ahead in the dark, very faintly, someone is knocking on stone.

If the clock is at 2 or more, a tremor jams the cage twenty feet short of the gallery: DC 14 Athletics to climb down the cables, or thieves'/tinker's tools to free the brake (Boon has expertise). On a failure, the cage drops free and slams down: 2d6 bludgeoning to everyone inside.

The fall

The Ninth Gallery runs away from the shaft into the mountain, low and straight as an arrow, so straight that your lamplight can't find the end of it. Rails gleam underfoot through a skin of black water. Timber props line the walls every few paces, and they're talking: creaking, ticking, groaning, the small complaining sounds of wood holding up a mountain and not enjoying it. Dust sifts down from the ceiling in thin, steady threads, and the threads sway, all together, as the mountain breathes.

Sixty yards in, the tunnel ends in a slope of broken rock that fills it from floor to ceiling. A cart lies crushed under the edge of it, one wheel still turning, slowly, in the water. And from behind the rock, muffled, comes the knocking: three blows, a pause, three blows. The miner's signal. We're alive. Then a voice, faint and cracked and young, calling through a gap you can't see: "Hello? Is someone there? Ma? We can hear you. The air's going bad. Please hurry."

⚔ Hunger in the Walls Combat · 7,200 XP (10,800 with the guardians) · Low+ / Moderate

Something answers the miners' knocking. Not three blows: a grinding, from inside the wall to your left, like a millstone turning in the rock. A patch of the tunnel wall goes soft and dark and wet-looking, and a mouth pushes out of it. That's all it is at first, a mouth, wide as a barrel, ringed with teeth like chisels, set in the top of a lumpy body of grey-brown stone. Three arms unfold around it, each ending in a hooked claw. Three eyes, spaced evenly around its crown, roll toward you, and toward the glitter of your buckles and rings and the jeweler's kit at Orek's belt.

Another rises out of the floor, through the black water, without a ripple. A third pours out of the ceiling. They're thin, these things, starved thin, their stone hides pitted, and they move with the twitchy urgency of animals that have been driven out of their feeding grounds by something bigger. They've smelled gems. They've smelled metal. And you're standing in a dead-end tunnel, holding a lamp.

Battle map prompt · The Ninth Gallery (40 × 16 squares)

Top-down orthographic fantasy battle map for a virtual tabletop, hand-painted digital illustration, lush and intricately detailed, saturated jewel-tone palette with deep contrasting shadows, dramatic glowing light sources casting colored pools of light, rich textures on stone, timber, moss and water, crisp readable shapes that stay clear under tokens, flat overhead view with no perspective tilt, medieval fantasy setting. A long horizontal map of a freshly cut dwarven mine tunnel deep underground, laid out for a 40 by 16 square grid. At the far left, a square timber shaft landing with an iron cage and coiled cable. Iron rail tracks run the length of the tunnel through shallow, glossy black water. Squared timber props line both walls at regular intervals, a few cracked and leaning. Two side alcoves hold a tool rack, barrels and a powder crate. Across the middle third, a sloping rockfall of broken stone blocks the tunnel, a crushed mine cart under its edge, with a small dry air pocket chamber just beyond it. Past the rockfall the tunnel continues to the far right edge, where the rough rock meets enormous, perfectly smooth ancient stone blocks; a scorched star-shaped breach in them is plugged by a bulging wall of smooth grey stone laced with glowing pale violet crystal veins. Hanging brass oil lamps cast amber pools; violet light glows at the far end. No people, no creatures, no text, letters, numbers or symbols, no grid lines, no modern objects.

Soundtrack prompt · Combat loop · Hunger in the Walls

An orchestral ambient soundtrack of a claustrophobic battle in a flooded mine tunnel against starving creatures that swim through solid rock, performed by a full live symphony orchestra: skittering col legno and pizzicato strings, low clarinets and bassoons growling, sudden timpani and bass drum bursts as the walls give way, tremolo cellos and violas building tension, a desperate horn call that keeps rising, sharp xylophone accents like teeth on stone. Tense, scrabbling, urgent. 128 BPM, C-sharp minor. Real acoustic instruments, concert-hall reverb, no synthesizers, no pads, no electronic sounds. Loopable, instrumental, no vocals.

Encounter · Hunger in the Walls4 Xorns (SRD)7,200 XP
Foes
Xorn ×4 (SRD: AC 19, HP 73, burrow 20 ft, Earth Glide, Treasure Sense). Three emerge when step 1 succeeds; the fourth comes up through the rockfall in round 3, on the miners' side.
Behavior
Starving, driven up from below. They go for whoever carries the most gems and precious metal: Vali (mithral plate, Sun Blade) and Orek (jeweler's kit) first. Each one flees into the rock at 25 HP or less.
The rescue
The three rescue steps below are actions taken during the fight. If the fight runs past round 5 before step 3 is done, the miners' air is nearly gone: Tam is unconscious when they reach him, and the clock ticks +1.
Bribes
A bonus action to toss a gem, a ring or 50+ gp of coin: the nearest xorn spends its next turn eating it. Orek's jeweler's kit holds about six good stones.
Terrain
  • Timber props: half cover. Knocking one out (an action, or a hit for 15+ damage) drops a 10-ft square of ceiling: DC 15 Dex save, 3d10 bludgeoning. Xorns in the rock under it are unharmed and annoyed.
  • Black water: difficult terrain along the rails. A xorn surfacing through it gets advantage on its first attack.
  • The rail cart: push it down the slope toward the rockfall (DC 13 Athletics): 3d6 bludgeoning in a 15-ft line.
  • The powder crate in the alcove: Boon can turn it into a trap (an action with tinker's tools): the next creature to enter that square triggers a 15-ft blast, 4d6 fire and bludgeoning, DC 15 Dex for half.
  • The rockfall: difficult terrain, and Earth Glide lets the xorns move straight through it.
Second wave
When anyone reaches the breach, the two dream-guardians step out of the sealing wall (unless the rune-token is shown). Run them as a fresh fight, or let them join this one if the xorns are still up.
Spotlight
Boon the precision blast mid-fight and the powder-crate trap · Vali the Immovable Rod under the fault while xorns chew at his armor · Orek tremorsense on things that move through stone, and tossing his own gems to save a life
Battlefield twists · the gallery is coming downRun alongside the fight
WhenTwistEffect
Always · swimmers in stoneA xorn inside the rock can't be seen or targetedIt surfaces to attack and gets advantage if it surfaces next to its target. Tremorsense counters it: Boon or Orek using Stonecunning (bonus action) knows where every submerged xorn is and can call it out, so allies can ready attacks for the moment it surfaces.
Always · they eat metalA xorn that crits Vali chews his armorThe mithral plate loses 1 AC until repaired (Boon can fix it with smith's or tinker's tools during a short rest). The Sun Blade, if dropped, is the first thing they go for.
Each round · initiative 0The mountain breathes: roll d61–2 nothing · 3–4 dust: every lamp gutters, dim light until the end of the next round (the dwarves don't care; Vali does, unless the Sun Blade is lit) · 5 water surge along the rails: DC 13 Dex save or prone · 6 a prop fails: a random 10-ft section of ceiling drops, DC 15 Dex save, 3d10 bludgeoning, half on a success
Round 3The fourth xorn breaks through on the miners' sideThe trapped men start screaming. Whoever opens the fall (step 3) now opens it onto a fight.
Round 4The water risesThe black water reaches knee height on a goliath, waist height on a dwarf: difficult terrain everywhere off the rail bed, and disadvantage on Dex saves for anyone standing in it.
Round 6The fault goesIf step 2 (hold the roof) isn't done, the middle 20 ft of the gallery comes down: DC 17 Dex save, 6d10 bludgeoning, half on a success. The xorns don't care. The rescue becomes a dig (clock +1).
The rescueSkill sequence · 3 steps · each an action during the fightIf the clock is at 2+: all DCs +2 (bad air)

Four men behind a wall of rock, a ceiling that wants to come down, and air running out. Who does what?

StepCheckResult
1 · Find them. Where's the air pocket, and where are the faults?Auto with Stonecunning tremorsense (Boon or Orek) · else DC 13 Perception or SurvivalSuccess: four heartbeats, faint, in a pocket ten feet back, and a fault line running above it like a crack in an eggshell. The next step knows where not to push. Failure: they dig in the wrong place first. Clock +1.
2 · Hold the roof. The props won't take what's coming.Vali's Immovable Rod under the fault (auto) · DC 17 Athletics (advantage in Large Form) · Boon's protector cannon gives advantageSuccess: the ceiling settles onto the rod or a pair of shoulders with a groan like a ship's keel, and holds. Dust pours down and stops. Failure: a slab drops. Everyone in the gallery, DC 15 Dex save, 3d10 bludgeoning, half on a success. Clock +1 while they shore it up by hand.
3 · Open the fall. Clear it without bringing the rest down on the men behind it.Boon with a charge: thieves' or tinker's tools DC 16 (expertise) · anyone else, DC 18 Arcana or tools · or dig by hand: group DC 14 AthleticsSuccess: read "The way through." Failure: the blast is too big, or the dig too slow. The men live, but Tam's leg is broken under a falling stone (by hand: clock +1).

Boon packs the charge into the crack the way you'd fit a key in a lock, and shapes it with your thumbs, and runs the fuse, and you all press yourselves against the props as it goes. The sound isn't a bang. It's a cough, flat and small, and a single neat hole the width of a dwarf punches through the fall with the rest of the rock standing around it, untouched, like a doorway somebody carved. Through it, in a haze of dust, four filthy faces turn toward the light. The youngest is barely more than a boy, with Ragna's jaw and somebody else's eyes. He looks at the man who made that hole, and at the bracelet on his wrist, and he knows exactly who you are. Everyone in Bagathorn grows up knowing. "You're him," Tam Deepcut says. Then, after a moment: "That was a good hole."

What Tam saw

Tam drinks half a waterskin in one go, coughs, and wipes his mouth. "Two nights back, we were on late shift down here, cutting toward nothing, like always. Master Dorn came down. On his own, at the second bell, which he never does. Said to knock off early, he'd inspect the props himself. He had gloves on." He frowns. "Thick ones. Indoors. And he was shaking. I thought it was the cold." He looks down the gallery toward the dark end. "We heard the bang from the cage. Brokk said it was a prop going."

The breach

Past the fall, the Ninth Gallery runs on for another hundred yards, and then it stops, and the place where it stops is wrong. The rough, pick-scarred dwarven tunnel runs straight into a wall of stone that nobody in Bagathorn cut: smooth as river ice, perfectly flat, made of blocks so enormous that a single seam runs from floor to ceiling and beyond. Somebody blew a hole in it. You can see the scorch, a ragged black star, and the shattered edge of the blocks around it.

And something has filled the hole back in. A plug of new stone bulges out of the breach like wax that has dripped and set, grey and smooth and still faintly warm when you put your hand on it, warm as skin. Veins of pale violet crystal run through it, and they glow, and they dim, and they glow again, slowly, in time with the breathing you've been feeling all night. You're close now. On the other side of this wall, something enormous breathes in, and holds it, and lets it out.

Reading the scene

Let them work it like detectives. Each line below is one clue; give it on the check or to the right PC automatically.

The breach · forensics
The chargeBoon: automatic others DC 14 Investigation Brass splinters, wire, the remains of a rune-etched casing. Boon knows it the way you know your own handwriting: the Gultor Lattice, his own shaped charge, built from his designs. Read "His own hand," below.
The sealDC 15 Arcana Orek: advantage The lattice was closed with a spoken incantation; the residue is verbal and somatic. Boon's original used a clockwork trigger, because Boon can't cast without tools. Whoever set this can cast with their own voice.
The inkDC 13 Perception A thumb-smear of blue-black ink on the blasted edge, glittering with grit. Orek knows the grit at a glance: crushed fire opal, ground fine, the grade your father sells by the ounce to scribes who want their seals to shine. The Gultors' pact ink.
The HushDC 15 Perception In the water by the wall: a bead of black wax wrapped in fine silver wire, cracked open and spent. Stamped into the wax, a tiny closed eye. DC 12 History for anyone who's walked the Nexus Bazaar: that's the mark of a stall there. Corvane's.
The tracksDC 14 Survival One dwarf, fine city boots with no hobnails, there and back. A short stride. Twice the prints stop and turn in place, as if the walker stood still for a long time.
The sliverDC 12 Perception A thumbnail chip of violet-black crystal blasted off the Eye, lying in the water, glowing faintly. Who touches it matters (below).

His own hand Boon

Boon, you turn a twist of the casing over in your fingers. You know every line of it. You drew these runes at sixteen, in the margins of your father's books, by candlelight, a hundred times, until they were right. And there is the binding rune, at the heart of the lattice: the one that tells all that force which way to go. It's drawn the right way up. The way you drew it in your workbook. The way you always thought you'd drawn it, before the day the gallery came down on three men and they showed you the casing from that bomb with the rune upside down, and you spent thirty years in a cell believing your own hand had done it. Whoever built this charge copied your workbook. And your workbook was right.

A seed, not the reveal. The truth is in Dorn's journal (Scene 4).

Touching the sliver

Orek (or any caster)

The sliver drinks. You feel it find the magic in you, the magic you never asked for, and pull, like a tide going out, and pour something back in. A dream: you are enormous and very old and lying in the warm dark, and a small figure is standing at your open hand, weeping. Gloved hands. A signet ring on one finger, a lamp-and-giant seal. It takes the light out of your palm, and the dark gets colder. DC 15 Wis save or fall asleep for 1 minute (an ally can shake them awake as an action).

Vali

The dream reaches for you the way it reaches for anyone with magic in them, and then it stops, and pulls back, like a hand from a hot stove. For one moment you feel the Sleeper's attention on you, vast and slow and puzzled, and very faintly displeased, as if she has found something in you that she does not like the smell of. Then she lets you go. (Vali's patron [OPEN].)

Boon

Nothing. It sits in your palm like a pebble. A little warm. A little pretty. You can feel it searching, the way you can feel a cat pushing at a closed door, and finding nothing to push through, and giving up. Everyone else who touched it went pale. You could carry it all day.

That's the clue: the Eye can't drink from a man the weave can't pass through. Boon is the only one who can carry it safely in Scene 5.

⚔ The dream-guardians Second wave · 3,600 XP

The violet veins in the sealing wall flare, all at once, bright enough to throw your shadows down the tunnel. The smooth grey stone bulges outward, and outward again, the way a blanket does when someone sits up under it. Two shapes push out of the wall, shedding gravel: tall and blunt and featureless, like statues somebody started and gave up on, with a seam of violet light where a face should be. They don't make a sound. They take one step toward you, and the floor of the Ninth Gallery cracks under their feet. In Giant, from somewhere inside the stone, a voice like a rockslide whispers: "Go back up into the dream, little ones. She is sleeping."

Vali holds up the rune-tokenThey stop, bow, and sink back into the wall. No fight.
Someone answers in GiantDC 15 Persuasion: they withdraw. On a failure, they attack.
Otherwise (the default)Two Earth Elementals (SRD), reskinned: their slams carry the dream (a creature hit makes a DC 13 Wis save or loses its reaction until its next turn). They move through the sealing wall freely and withdraw into it at half HP. They drive intruders off; they don't chase.
Quick reference · the Gultor Shaft & the Ninth Gallery
Look closerThe survey charter on the shack wall. Four empty lamp pegs (30 is Tam's; 12 has been empty for thirty-one years). Violet veins in the shaft walls on the way down, thicker the deeper you go.
SensesSap on new timber · groaning props, dripping water, three knocks · lamp oil, wet stone, a sweet church-smell from below · warm air, cold water to the ankles · stone that's warm as skin
Who's hereTam Deepcut: nineteen, Ragna's son. Born the year his father died. Saw Dorn come down with gloves on.Pim Hollin, Old Gorrin, Sedda Coalbright: the other three miners. Gorrin was on shift the day Olin died; he won't look at Boon.Ragna and Brokk: see their cards.
Rumors"Brokk says the Ninth was dug crooked on purpose" (it was dug dead straight, on purpose) · "Something sings behind the wall at night" (true: the guardians)
On returnAfter clock 6: the sealing wall has cracked down the middle, and violet light pours out of it into the gallery. The way into the hall is open.
Stat noteXorns: Xorn ×4 (SRD), flee at 25 HP. Dream-guardians: Earth Elemental ×2 (SRD), retreat at half HP.

Ask the table

  • Boon, do you take the lamp off the peg yourself, or leave it?
  • Orek, the ink on that wall has your family's trade in it. What goes through your head?
  • Vali, the Sleeper didn't like what she found in you. Do you know what she found?

If the party…

Tries to dig through the sealing wallIt heals as fast as they cut, warm and wet as a wound closing. It opens at clock 6, or for the rune-token and a sung line of the lullaby.

Clues: the Lattice (copied from Boon's workbook, sealed with a spoken spell); Gultor ink; a Nexus Bazaar Hush; Dorn's survey and his gloves; the Eye can't drink from BoonClock: +2 as they leave (more on failures)

Along the ledge to the pitheadGo to Scene 2 →

NudgeThe guardians' whisper was in Giant, and the party still doesn't know what was taken. Brokk: "Them three up at the Deepdelve have been sitting there since sundown. If anyone knows what's behind that wall, it's them."

The cage hauls you back up into the cold, and the crowd at the shaft head surges forward to meet the miners, and nobody notices you leave. Brokk points you along a miners' ledge that runs across the face of the mountain toward the old mine. It's barely wider than a cart, the town's lights far below on one side and black rock on the other. A loose stone turns under your boot and goes over the edge and you never hear it land. Up ahead the ledge bends around a buttress of rock, and on the far side it joins the broad, cart-worn stones of the Ore Road just below its last bend, where nothing at all is moving.

Then read the Scene 2 arrival.

Down to the towerGo to Scene 4 →

NudgeTam: "Master Dorn had gloves on." The charter: "certified by D. Gultor." And Boon's own workbook, which was locked in his father's house the day they took him away. Everything points to the black tower.

You come down off the mountain by the miners' way, a goat path of switchbacks that drops straight toward the top of the town, loose stone sliding under your boots, the cold scouring the mine's warm air out of your lungs. Below you Bagathorn is in motion: lamps bobbing along every street toward the pass road, a long, slow river of light leaving the town. The path lets you out behind the old houses of the highest tier, where the streets are wide and empty, and an alley brings you out at the foot of the Consul's Stair. You climb the last flight.

Then read the Scene 4 arrival.

Through the wallGo to Scene 5 →

NudgeAt clock 6, or if they open the wall with the rune-token and the lullaby. Every violet vein in the plug flares, and a sound like a great bell cracking runs through the stone. Whoever touched the sliver hears, in the dream, a man's voice weeping, very close now.

The sealing wall splits from top to bottom with a sound like a frozen lake breaking, and the two halves slump apart, soft as wax, and through the gap pours light the color of a bruise. You step through the breach, over the scorched blocks, out of the dwarven tunnel and into a passage cut for something many times your size. Its floor is worn into a shallow bowl. Its walls are carved, all the way up into the dark, with the same figure over and over: a giant, lying down, asleep. The air is as warm as breath. The breathing is louder here. It isn't under you anymore. Ahead, the passage opens out.

Then read the Scene 5 arrival.
