4

The House of Gultor

Small hoursThe Gultor Tower, highest tier
Who: Fennick Gultor, Dorn Gultor, Bramm Gultor, Old PellLeans on: Boon Orek Vali
Why they're here
  • Fennick asked Boon to come, "not here, not with Father listening" (Scene 1).
  • The thief is a Gultor (Scene 2). The charter says "D. Gultor"; Tam saw Dorn's gloves (Scene 3).
  • Boon's workbook was locked in this house the day they took him away.

The scene's job: the investigation pays off. Search the study, read Dorn, find the old journal, and give Boon and his father their one quiet moment. When Dorn is exposed, the Eye takes him down into the mountain (in the middle of a fight, if you run the optional Hushed). Clock +1 when the scene ends.

Art prompt · The Gultor Tower

Painterly dark-fantasy concept art, deep-mountain noir, cold blue-grey granite and soot-black shadow cut by warm amber lantern light, veins of pale opalescent violet glowing in the stone, drifting rock dust in the air, cinematic composition, highly detailed environment, 16:9 aspect ratio. A slim, tall tower of black basalt standing alone on the highest terrace of a dwarven mountain town at night, its walls fluted like organ pipes, crowned by a dome of green-weathered brass with a telescope slit glowing amber. Narrow lancet windows lit on every floor. A heavy iron-studded door under a carved stone lintel showing a dwarf with a lamp facing a sleeping giant. Worn stone steps leading up to it, frost on the railings. Below and behind, the terraces of the town fall away toward a river of moving lamplight on a mountain road. Stars, cold mist, the mountain looming. Proud, lonely, secretive. No people, no text, no watermark.

Art prompt · Dorn's study under the dome

Painterly dark-fantasy concept art, deep-mountain noir, cold blue-grey granite and soot-black shadow cut by warm amber lantern light, veins of pale opalescent violet glowing in the stone, drifting rock dust in the air, cinematic composition, highly detailed environment, 16:9 aspect ratio. A round scholar's study at the top of a basalt tower, under a ribbed brass dome with a telescope pointed at the stars. At the center stands a great brass orrery of mountains and moons, its hollow central sphere hinged open and empty, faint violet light still clinging to its inner surface. A cluttered desk of black oak strewn with survey maps, an inkwell of glittering blue-black ink, a pair of thick leather gloves, a cracked crystal wand, a burnt-down candle. Shelves of ledgers, an old rolled map of a vast underground hall pinned flat with stones. A cold hearth, scattered pages, a narrow window showing lamplight moving on a road far below. Hushed, guilty, abandoned in haste. No people, no text, no watermark.

Soundtrack prompt · The House of Gultor

An orchestral ambient soundtrack of a proud old family's tower in the small hours, full of secrets and grief, performed by a live chamber orchestra: a slow, aching solo cello melody over soft sustained violas, a hesitant piano-less harp figure like a clock ticking in an empty room, a bassoon and clarinet in quiet, uneasy dialogue, and a single high violin line that rises and falls back unanswered. Intimate, sorrowful, suspicious. 58 BPM, B minor. Real acoustic instruments, concert-hall reverb, no synthesizers, no pads, no electronic sounds. Loopable, instrumental, no vocals.

The Gultor Tower stands on the highest tier of Bagathorn like a finger raised for silence. It's taller than anything around it and thinner than it has any right to be, black basalt fluted like the pipes of an organ, rising to a dome of brass gone green with weather, a telescope slit glowing amber at the top. Every window is lit, one above another, all the way up, a column of small gold squares against the bulk of the mountain.

Up here the town is quiet. The great houses of the old families stand dark and shuttered around a square of frosted cobbles; their owners left hours ago, early and well-organized, the way the rich always leave. Below the terrace's edge, the rest of Bagathorn is moving: a long river of lamplight crawling up the pass road out of town, so slowly you can't see it move unless you look away and back. Somewhere down there a dog is barking and won't stop.

Over the tower door, the lintel is carved with a scene worn soft by three hundred winters: a small figure with a lamp, standing before a vast shape lying on its side. Boon, you used to think it was a dwarf and a mountain. The iron-studded door opens before anyone knocks, and an ancient, tiny woman in a housekeeper's cap peers up at you over a candle, and her face crumples. "Master Boon," says Old Pell. "Oh, look at you. Your room's aired. It's always aired. Your father has me do it Tuesdays."

Fennick

Fennick is waiting in the archive on the third floor, a long, low room of shelves and ledgers that smells of dust and lamp oil and the bitter, mineral scent of the family's blue-black ink. He's lit too many candles. He's pacing between them. When you come in he stops, takes off his spectacles, polishes them on a shirt that's buttoned wrong, puts them back on, and doesn't look any of you in the eye. "I didn't know who else to tell. Father won't hear it. The mayor would hang him. And you're the only one of us who's ever," he swallows, "who's ever been wrong in public and lived."

Fennick's secretRoleplayAuto if Boon speaks to him as a brother · else DC 13 Persuasion

He's terrified of saying it out loud, as if saying it will make it true. How do you get it out of him?

Success

"It's Dorn." It comes out in a rush, like a held breath. "His magic's going. Three weeks now. He tried to light the council lamps last week, a cantrip, he's done it since he was nine, and nothing came. He laughed it off. He's worn gloves ever since, indoors, even at supper. And two nights ago he went down the new shaft, alone, late, and came back at dawn white as chalk, and since then he's been," Fennick searches for the word, "better. Casting again. Better than ever. And humming. All the time, humming, like the mountain." He looks at Boon at last. "The Gultor gift doesn't skip, Boon. Father always said. It doesn't skip. It ends. I think it ended for him, and he couldn't bear it."

Failure

Fennick shakes his head, and shakes it again, and can't. "I can't. I can't be the one." He presses a key into Boon's hand: small, brass, old. "Dorn's study. Top of the tower. He's with Father at the council hall. Look for yourselves. Please don't make me say it."

Cost: clock +1 while they search unguided. They lose Fennick's testimony for now (he'll give it in front of Bramm in the quiet moment).

Dorn

Boots on the stair, quick and light, and a voice before a face: warm, rich, a voice made for council chambers. "Fennick, have you seen my…" Dorn Gultor stops in the archive doorway. He's the handsome one. He always was. Tall for a dwarf, beard braided with silver beads where his father wears copper, a coat of deep blue velvet cut by someone who charged for it. Thick black leather gloves on both hands. Around him, faintly, so faintly you might be imagining it, there's a hum, like a struck glass that never stops ringing.

His face does three things in a heartbeat: shock, then something that looks very much like fear, and then, smoothly, the most delighted smile you have ever seen. "Boon!" He crosses the room in three strides and throws his arms around his little brother, and holds on a beat too long. "Look at you. They let you out. Gods, it's been, what, thirty years?" He steps back, hands on Boon's shoulders, beaming. Through the leather of his gloves, his grip is cold and hard as a pair of stone clamps. "And you've brought friends. Detectives! Good. Good. The mountain needs all the help it can get. I've been up all night working on a ward to calm it."

Dorn Gultor new
Eldest son and heir to the consultancy · the thief · charming, brilliant, terrified · Friendly (performed)
Look
Handsome, blue velvet, silver beads, thick gloves. Under the gloves: grey stone veins climbing from his fingertips to his wrists, and rising.
Voice
Warm, practiced, a beat too fast. Touches people when he lies.
Wants
To keep casting. To be the son his father believed in. To give the Eye back, and he can't make his hand let go.
Hiding
The Eye, in an inside pocket over his heart; its light shows through the velvet when he's afraid. And the thing he did to Boon's bomb thirty-one years ago.
Steers
Toward Mayor Durrin ("Hesk wanted that copper badly enough to dig through a god"). A red herring.

"You don't know what it's like, Boon. To have it, all your life, and feel it go."

Portrait prompt · Dorn Gultor (for an actor or token)

Painterly dark-fantasy character portrait, deep-mountain noir, cold blue-grey shadow cut by warm amber lamplight, drifting dust, highly detailed, 2:3 aspect ratio. A handsome middle-aged dwarf wizard in a tailored deep-blue velvet coat, his dark beard braided with small silver beads, smiling warmly with frightened eyes. He wears thick black leather gloves, and where one glove is pulled down at the wrist, his skin turns to grey stone shot through with fine glowing violet veins. A faint violet light shows through the velvet over his heart. Behind him, candlelit shelves of ledgers. Charming, brittle, cracking. No text, no watermark.

Dorn's answers · what he says, and what Insight sees
They askDorn saysTruth · DC 15 Insight Vali: advantage
Why the gloves?"Burned my hands on a ward-circle last week. Clumsy." He flexes them.Lie. He touched his face as he said it.
Why dig the Ninth?"The copper. Hesk was desperate for it. I gave him the bearing he asked for."Lie, and a nudge toward the mayor. He chose the bearing.
Where were you two nights ago?"Here. Working. Ask Pell." (Pell, later: "He went out after the second bell. I heard the door.")Lie.
Do you know the pact-word?"Father's never trusted me with it." A laugh.Lie. Bramm gave it to him at twenty-one, as heir.
What's that humming?"The mountain. Can't you hear it? Everyone's humming tonight."True, and not the answer. The Eye is singing against his heart.
Show us your hands.A long pause. "No."The first true thing he's said.

If the party isn't ready to confront him, Dorn excuses himself ("the council needs me") and leaves the tower. He comes back at clock 6, or the Eye takes him down then, wherever he is.

The study

The top of the tower is one round room under the brass dome, a great telescope angled at the stars through the open slit, the night air pouring in, cold. In the middle of the floor stands an orrery taller than Vali: mountains of brass and moons of polished stone on long arms, all turning around a hollow central sphere. The sphere is hinged open. It's empty. Its inside is lined with velvet, and the velvet is still faintly warm, and it glows, very faintly, a violet that fades as you watch, like the afterimage of a lamp you've just blown out. The desk is a ruin of maps and papers. On top of them lies a crystal wand, cracked clean through.

Searching the study · each find is one clue
The receiptDC 12 Investigation Tucked in the blotter. Handout below. The same closed eye as the Hush at the breach.
The letterOrek: automatic others DC 14 A folded letter under a paperweight, sealed with a gemcutter's mark Orek has known his whole life. Handout and read-aloud below.
Dorn's notesDC 13 Investigation A ledger of failing magic and what the Eye does to him. Handout below. "A dry man could carry it like a pebble."
Haldra's papersDC 14 History A brittle map of the giants' hall: the bed, the Sleeper, a socket drawn in her open palm "cut to fit one way only." On the back, in Haldra's hand, the Stone-Lullaby (if they didn't get it in Scene 2).
The workbookDC 15 thieves' tools Boon: expertise A locked drawer. Inside, Boon's own workbook, confiscated thirty-one years ago. The Lattice pages are thumbed soft, with fresh notes in Dorn's hand: "Closes with a spoken binding. Simple. Why did he never…? Oh. He couldn't."
A second HushDC 15 Perception In a snuffbox: an unspent Hush of the Deep. Dorn bought two.
HiddenDC 17 Investigation Orek: +13 The desk's bottom drawer is two fingers too shallow. Under a false floor: a cheap, water-stained journal, thirty-one years old. Read "The journal," below.
Handout · the receipt
THE CLOSED EYE · Nexus Bazaar, Third Ring
Sold to: D.G., Bagathorn
2 × Hush of the Deep (silences heart & step; giant-ward grade)
Paid: one signet, lamp-and-giant seal, gold, 300 yrs+
"A pleasure, Consultant. Come back when you need to be quieter still." — C.

Dorn paid with Haldra's pact-seal ring, the oldest thing the family owned. Corvane now has it. Seizing this receipt and showing it to Seraphine keeps the Corvane clock from ticking.

Handout · the letter, sealed with the Opaldigger mark
Master Gultor,
You describe a stone the size of a fist, black, with lights that move, which "hums." I will not appraise it. I will not buy it, broker it, cut it or look at it. No Opaldigger touches a stone that sings, and no honest cutter touches a stone that came out of the dark without its owner's leave. Take it back where you found it.
— Yardim Opaldigger

Orek, you know that hand. You learned your letters copying it. Every stroke of it is the same as it was when he stood over you at the kitchen table, tapping the page, making you write out the properties of beryl for the hundredth time when you wanted to be outside with a stick for a sword. You've spent your whole life knowing exactly who your father is: the man who wanted a mage for a son and wouldn't take no. You didn't know he was the kind of man who'd turn away a fortune because it wasn't honest. It's a strange thing, at your age, to learn something new about your father from a letter he wrote to somebody else.

Handout · Dorn's notes (torn from a ledger)
Day 1. Lamp cantrip failed at council. Laughed it off.
Day 9. Nothing. Not even a spark. Father mustn't know.
Day 14. Haldra's map. The Eye. It lets the holder cast THROUGH it. No weave in the body needed.
Day 22. I have it. I can cast again. Better than ever.
Day 23. It drinks the weave through the body and pours her dream back. A dry man could carry it like a pebble. I am not a dry man. Fingers grey to the second knuckle.
Day 24. I'll take it back tonight. Tonight.

The journal Boon

Handout · a water-stained journal, thirty-one years old
Father talked about nothing but B.'s devices at supper again. "A new kind of magic," he called it. B. can't even light a candle.

I turned the binding rune on the Lattice charge he made for the Seventh. Only turned it. It will fizzle in front of the whole crew and Father will see his toys are dangerous.

(later, the ink shaking) No one was supposed to be in the gallery. No one was supposed to be in the gallery. No one was supposed to

Softer version [OPEN]: replace the middle paragraph with "I saw the binding rune on B.'s charge was upside down. I said nothing. Let Father see his toys are dangerous."

Don't read anything aloud after this handout. Let Boon's player have the silence. Then ask: "What do you do with that?"

Quiet moment · Boon's room

Play this whenever Boon and Bramm are in the tower together: Bramm comes home from the council hall, or Boon goes looking for his old room. No rolls. Fennick can be in the doorway if he hasn't spoken yet.

Your room is exactly as it was. Old Pell wasn't lying: it's aired, and dusted, and someone has wound the little brass clock on the shelf, the one you built at twelve that tells the time by ringing a different note on every hour. The shelves are still full of your mistakes: a clockwork beetle with one leg, a lamp that lit itself with a spring and a flint, a music box that only ever played the first four notes of anything. On the desk, a sheet of paper with a rune-lattice drawn on it in a child's careful hand, and beside it, in a different hand, an old man's hand, a small neat correction, and the word good.

Bramm is sitting on the edge of your bed with his staff across his knees. He has been sitting there, you think, for some time. He doesn't stand up when you come in. "I come in here on Tuesdays," he says. "Pell thinks I come to check she's done it properly."

He looks at the shelves for a long while. "I could feel the weave in you, Boon. When you were small. All around you, like heat off a stone. It just never came out of your hands. I thought it was stubbornness. I thought if I pushed hard enough…" He stops. "I taught you everything I knew. It was the wrong everything. You found the right one on your own, and I never told you it was magic, because it didn't look like mine."

The little brass clock on the shelf rings one note, and stops. "I never believed you drew that rune wrong," your father says, very quietly. "I knew your hand. I said nothing, because the other answer was worse." He looks up at you, and for the first time tonight, his face moves. "Son. I'm sorry."

Let it breathe · no rolls

  • Boon: what do you say to him? Or do you say nothing?
  • If they've found the journal: does Boon show it to him?
  • Bramm, if asked, gives the pact-word clue: "Haldra's word is given to the heir at twenty-one. I gave it to Dorn." And the way down: "There is a stair under this tower that only Gultor blood can open. Haldra used it to visit them."

From the dome Valioptional

Vali, from the telescope slit you can see the whole town below, and the long crawl of lamps up the pass road. You can see them close enough, through the glass, to make out faces. A woman carrying two children, one on each hip. A boy of perhaps eight pulling a smaller girl along by the hand, no adults near them, the girl crying, the boy not, his jaw set, his eyes fixed on the road ahead the way a soldier's are. Somebody's village is burning, in a way. Somebody's children are walking away from it in the dark, on their own.

Optional fight · The Hushed11,700 XP · ModerateCorvane's silent assassins come for the Eye. The twist: the party can't hear them, tremorsense can feel them, and in round 3 the stone takes Dorn from the middle of the fight.

Trigger: the moment the party confronts Dorn, or the first time they search the study with him nearby. Corvane sold Dorn the Hush; now Corvane wants what Dorn bought it for. Skip it, and the Corvane thread still lands through the receipt and the closing note.

The candles go out. Not blown, not guttered: every flame in the room simply stops, as if the air itself had held its breath, and in the sudden dark the only light is the cold starlight falling through the telescope slit and the violet glow under Dorn's coat. You didn't hear anything. That's what's wrong. The wind was whistling through the slit a moment ago. Now there is no sound at all: not the wind, not the clock, not your own breathing. The silence has edges.

Three figures are in the room. You don't know how long they've been there. They're dressed in close-fitting grey, and where their faces should be there are smooth masks of black wax, each with a single closed eye pressed into the forehead, and they move without making a sound, without stirring the papers on the floor, without a footfall. One is already behind Dorn. A blade the color of a bruise comes up toward his throat, and a gloved hand reaches for the light inside his coat.

Battle map prompt · Dorn's study under the dome (24 × 24 squares)

Top-down orthographic fantasy battle map for a virtual tabletop, hand-painted digital illustration, lush and intricately detailed, saturated jewel-tone palette with deep contrasting shadows, dramatic glowing light sources casting colored pools of light, rich textures on stone, timber, moss and water, crisp readable shapes that stay clear under tokens, flat overhead view with no perspective tilt, medieval fantasy setting. A square map of a circular scholar's observatory at the top of a black basalt tower, laid out for a 24 by 24 square grid, the round room filling most of the map with dark night-sky void in the corners. A polished basalt floor inlaid with a ring of brass. At the center, a large brass orrery seen from above: a hollow sphere hinged open and glowing faint violet inside, surrounded by long radiating brass arms holding stone moons and mountains. A brass telescope on a circular rotating platform points toward a narrow slit opening in the north wall, where starlight falls across the floor. A heavy black oak desk heaped with maps, papers, an inkwell and candles near the east wall. Tall bookshelves follow the curved walls, one leaning. A cold stone hearth on the west side, a woven rug, scattered loose pages, and a spiral stair opening in the south. Amber candlelight pools, cold blue starlight, violet glow. No people, no creatures, no text, letters, numbers or symbols, no grid lines, no modern objects.

Soundtrack prompt · Combat loop · The Hushed

An orchestral ambient soundtrack of a deadly fight against silent masked assassins in a dark tower observatory lit by starlight, performed by a full live symphony orchestra: hushed, tense pizzicato strings and col legno taps, brushed timpani, a nervous solo clarinet weaving through, low muted brass stabs, sudden sforzando string hits like knife strikes, then a fierce, driving cello and viola ostinato as the fight erupts. Stealthy, noir, lethal. 116 BPM, F-sharp minor. Real acoustic instruments, concert-hall reverb, no synthesizers, no pads, no electronic sounds. Loopable, instrumental, no vocals.

Encounter · The Hushed3 Assassins (SRD)11,700 XP
Foes
Assassin ×3 (SRD: AC 15, HP 78, two shortsword attacks with poison, Sneak Attack, Assassinate). Each wears a Hush of the Deep: completely silent, advantage on Stealth, and the party is surprised unless someone was actively watching the slit or the stair.
The counter
Tremorsense beats the Hush. Boon or Orek can use Stonecunning (bonus action) to feel every footstep on the basalt floor: no advantage from unseen attackers against them, and they can point targets out to Vali. Divine Sense doesn't help (they're mortals).
Goal
They want the Eye, not the party. Round 1, one goes for Dorn (he has AC 16, 120 HP, and two Dream-Shard bolts; he defends himself and nothing else). Grabbing the Eye burns them like anyone else (3d10 psychic), so they try to take Dorn with it, gagged and dragged to the slit.
The stone takes him
At the end of round 3, or when Dorn drops below 60 HP, read "The stone takes him" mid-fight. The assassins left standing fight one more round, then go for the slit and their grapnel lines down the tower. A captured one talks (below).
Terrain
  • The orrery: an action and DC 14 Athletics spins it. Everything within 10 ft makes a DC 14 Dex save or takes 2d10 bludgeoning and is pushed 10 ft.
  • The telescope: heavy brass on a pivot. Swing it (an action) to make a +7 melee attack against a creature within 10 ft of the platform: 2d8 bludgeoning, knocked prone.
  • The slit: a creature shoved through it is hanging from the outside of the tower 80 ft up (DC 15 Athletics each turn to hold on).
  • The spiral stair: shoved down it, 2d6 bludgeoning and out of the fight for a round.
  • The bookshelves: topple one (DC 15 Athletics): 3d6 bludgeoning in a 10-ft line, restrained until freed.
  • The desk and papers: half cover. One fire spell and the papers go up: the clues on the desk burn unless someone grabs them (an action).
  • Darkness: the candles are out. Starlight from the slit is dim light; the Sun Blade changes everything.
Spotlight
Vali the Sun Blade blazing in a dark room, standing over Dorn whatever he's done · Orek tremorsense on silent feet, Goading Attack to draw them off Dorn · Boon tremorsense, Flash of Genius on a poison save, a cannon in a cramped room

A captured Hushed talks · DC 15 Intimidation

The wax mask comes off: an ordinary, frightened face. "We work for the Closed Eye. Corvane. In the Nexus. He said the ring was a down payment, and the stone was the real sale. He has a buyer." (True. The buyer is [OPEN].) If they let him go, the Corvane clock ticks +1. If they hand him to Seraphine, it doesn't.

Loot from the Hushed

Each carries a spent Hush, 40 gp in Nexus scrip, a grapnel and silk line, and a vial of the bruise-colored poison (one use: a weapon coated with it deals an extra 3d6 poison on the next hit, DC 15 Con for half).

The stone takes him

Read this when the party confronts Dorn, or at clock 6 wherever he is (if he's not present, it happens in the cellar and they arrive in time to see it). If you're running the optional Hushed fight, read it at the end of round 3, or when Dorn drops below 60 HP.

Dorn's smile holds for a long moment after it has stopped meaning anything. Then he pulls off one glove, finger by finger, the way you'd take a bandage off a wound you already know is bad. His hand is grey. Not pale: grey, the grey of granite, and threaded through it are fine veins of violet light that pulse, slowly, in time with the mountain. The stone climbs past his wrist and vanishes into his sleeve. Over his heart, through the blue velvet, a violet glow swells and fades, swells and fades.

"I was going to take it back," he says. His voice cracks down the middle. "I went down tonight. I stood at her hand. I couldn't open my fingers." He looks at Boon, and his eyes are wet, and for the first time all night he isn't performing. "You don't know what it's like. To have it all your life, and feel it go. To wake up and be… ordinary." He laughs, horribly. "No. You do. You're the only one who does. That's funny, isn't it? That's the funniest thing I've ever heard."

The floor under him softens. You see it happen: the flagstones go dark and glossy, like wet clay, and his boots sink into them to the ankle, then to the shin. He doesn't fight it. He looks down at the stone taking him with a kind of awful relief. "It wants to go home," he whispers. "And it won't let go of me." The violet light flares under his coat, bright enough to throw every shadow in the room against the walls, and the stone closes over Dorn Gultor's head like water, and he's gone. The floor is only floor. Somewhere far beneath your feet, the mountain breathes in, and holds it.

Clock: if it's below 6, set it to 6 (the Eye is home, and the Sleeper's eyes are opening). Go to Scene 5.

Quick reference · the Gultor Tower
LayoutGround: hall, kitchen, Pell's room. Second: Bramm's rooms and Boon's old room. Third: the archive. Top: Dorn's study under the dome. Cellar: a round door of black stone carved with the lamp-and-giant seal. It opens to Gultor blood or the pact-word; behind it, Haldra's stair goes down into the mountain.
SensesCandle smoke, dust, bitter mineral ink · the little brass clock ringing the hours · cold air pouring in through the telescope slit · a hum like a struck glass around Dorn
Who's hereOld Pell: housekeeper, ninety, raised all three boys. Heard Dorn go out after the second bell two nights ago. Calls Boon "Master Boon" and means it.Fennick, Dorn, Bramm: see their cards.
RumorsPell: "Master Dorn hasn't eaten in two days. Hums at his supper. Like the walls." (true)
On returnAfter Dorn is taken: a patch of floor that's warmer than the rest, and the cellar door standing open, violet light breathing up the stairs.

Ask the table

  • Boon: your brother just said you're the only one who understands. Is he right?
  • Orek: what do you do with your father's letter? Keep it?
  • Vali: everyone answers for what they did. What does Dorn owe, and to whom?

If the party…

Attacks Dorn in the towerHe casts once (a Dream-Shard bolt), then the stone takes him. Clock set to 6. (If you want a fight here, this is the moment to bring in the Hushed.)
Grabs for the Eye in his coatA non-Boon hand: 3d10 psychic and DC 16 Wis save or asleep 1 round, and the stone takes him anyway. Boon's hand closes on it, and it doesn't burn him, and Dorn screams "No!" and the floor swallows them both: Boon arrives in Scene 5 already beside the Sleeper, wrestling him.
Searches before Dorn arrivesHe walks in on them in the study, sees the open drawer, and the confrontation starts there.
Clues: Dorn's failing magic (Fennick, notes); Corvane's receipt; Yardim's letter; the socket and the lullaby (Haldra's map); the journal; "A dry man could carry it like a pebble"Clock: +1 as they leave (or set to 6 when the stone takes Dorn)Corvane clock: +1 if a captured Hushed goes free
Leads to · Scene 2 · 3 · 53 paths
Up the Ore RoadGo to Scene 2 →

NudgeBefore Dorn is exposed. Bramm, or Haldra's papers: "Only the giants can say what the Eye is, and how it must go back." The lamp-and-giant carving over the door points the way: the pact was made with them.

You leave the tower by the back gate, where a lane runs behind the great houses to the head of the Ore Road, and climb. The road is empty going up; everyone else in Bagathorn is going the other way. Halfway along, a cart has been abandoned with its load still in it, a dwarf's whole life roped down under a tarpaulin: a rocking chair, a spinning wheel, a cradle. You pass it without speaking. The slag heaps steam in the cold. The lights of the town sink away beneath you, and you climb the last switchback, onto a stretch of road where nobody has come in hours.

Then read the Scene 2 arrival.

To the Gultor ShaftGo to Scene 3 →

NudgeFennick: "The Gultor Shaft. That's where he went, two nights ago. And Ragna's boy is down there now." Old Pell, wringing her hands: "Ragna Deepcut. Oh, Master Boon. Of all the families."

A steep stair climbs from behind the tower, past the last houses and out onto the bare mountainside, where it turns into a path and the path turns into scree. The wind finds you up here, thin and bitter, and the cold is enough to make your teeth ache. Below and behind, the black finger of the tower shrinks, its windows still lit, one above another. Ahead, the slope rises toward a shelf of raw rock against the stars. You can hear voices before you can see anything: low, worn, a crowd that has been waiting a long time.

Then read the Scene 3 arrival.

Haldra's stairGo to Scene 5 →

NudgeAfter the stone takes Dorn. Bramm, gripping his staff: "The cellar. Haldra's door. It opens for Gultor blood." He looks at Boon. "It will open for you."

The cellar door is a disc of black stone taller than a goliath, carved with the same lamp and the same sleeping shape. Boon lays his palm on it, and the stone grows warm under his hand, and rolls aside without a sound. Beyond, a stair goes down, cut for dwarven feet, narrow and steep, and down, and down, past the tower's foundations, past the town's, into the mountain itself. Haldra's lamp-niches line the walls every hundred steps, empty for three centuries. The air grows warm. The breathing grows loud. At the bottom, the stair opens through a dwarf-sized door in an enormous wall, and beyond it, light the color of a bruise.

Then read the Scene 5 arrival.

sections.title: The Sleeper Wakes
sections.html:
5

The Sleeper Wakes

The last hour before dawnThe Hall of Ammaskar, deep in Mount Thurn
Who: Dorn Gultor, Ammaskar the Sleeper, two dream-guardians, Thrunna and Kolgrim (round 3)Leans on: Boon Orek Vali, one step each
Why they're here
  • The stone took Dorn down into the mountain, and Haldra's stair follows him (Scene 4).
  • Or the clock reached 6: the sealing wall cracked open (Scene 3), or Thrunna opened the giants' road (Scene 2).

The scene's job: the climax. Get the Eye out of Dorn's hand and back into Ammaskar's, and sing her down, before dawn. Then judge Dorn.

How the climax works · DM only
  • Rounds until dawn, from the clock as the scene starts: 5 or less = 6 rounds · 6 = 5 · 7 = 4 · 8 = 3 (Thrunna holds the mountain with her song for three rounds; she can do it once). Kolgrim singing (clock-7 effect live) costs one more round.
  • Four steps, one action each, in order (table below): take the Eye · carry it to her hand · seat it · sing her down. Anyone can attempt any step; each step has a PC it was built for.
  • The Eye drinks. Any creature with spellcasting that holds it takes 3d10 psychic at the start of each of its turns and makes a DC 16 Wis save or falls asleep until the end of its next turn. Boon is immune: there's no river in him to drink from.
  • The rune-token (Scene 2): held up, the dream-guardians turn on Dorn instead of the party.
  • Dorn doesn't have to die. Taking the Eye from him ends his fight: the stone stops climbing, and he collapses, weeping.
  • If the rounds run out, read "If dawn comes first."
Art prompt · The Hall of Ammaskar

Painterly dark-fantasy concept art, deep-mountain noir, cold blue-grey granite and soot-black shadow cut by warm amber lantern light, veins of pale opalescent violet glowing in the stone, drifting rock dust in the air, cinematic composition, highly detailed environment, 16:9 aspect ratio. A cathedral-sized cavern hollowed from the heart of a mountain, its far walls lost in darkness, its ceiling supported by colossal columns each carved as a giant lying asleep. In the center, on a raised bed of living rock, lies an immense elder stone giantess, sixty feet long, so ancient that moss, roots and clusters of glowing pale-violet crystal grow over her like a blanket, her face serene and lined like a cliff. Her right arm lies open at her side, palm up, with an empty, perfectly cut socket in the stone of her palm. Shafts of violet light rise from cracks in the floor; dust and grit fall in slow curtains from the ceiling; the floor is fractured in great plates. Overwhelming scale, sacred, on the edge of waking. No people, no text, no watermark.

Battle map prompt · The Hall of Ammaskar (40 × 30 squares)

Top-down orthographic fantasy battle map for a virtual tabletop, hand-painted digital illustration, lush and intricately detailed, saturated jewel-tone palette with deep contrasting shadows, dramatic glowing light sources casting colored pools of light, rich textures on stone, timber, moss and water, crisp readable shapes that stay clear under tokens, flat overhead view with no perspective tilt, medieval fantasy setting. A landscape map of a vast cavern hall in the heart of a mountain, laid out for a 40 by 30 square grid. In the center, a raised platform of living rock about twenty squares long holds an immense sleeping stone giantess seen from directly above, rendered entirely as weathered grey rock so she reads as part of the landscape: lying on her back with her head to the north, blanketed in green moss, pale roots and clusters of glowing violet crystal. Her right arm lies open beside the platform, palm up, with a small empty socket in the palm glowing violet. The cavern floor around her is broken into great tilted stone plates separated by glowing violet fissures. Colossal round pillar bases ring the edges of the hall, and clusters of violet crystal and fallen rubble give scattered cover. A small dwarf-sized doorway opens in the south wall; a rough split-rock passage enters from the east; an enormous sealed giant-sized door stands in the west wall. No people, no creatures, no text, letters, numbers or symbols, no grid lines, no modern objects.

Soundtrack prompt · The Sleeper Wakes

An orchestral ambient soundtrack of a desperate battle beside an enormous sleeping giantess who is waking up as a mountain begins to move, performed by a full live symphony orchestra: driving ostinato in low strings and timpani in 7/8, stabbing trombone and tuba chords like falling rock, frantic tremolo violins, a heroic French horn theme fighting upward, and every so often the old giants' lullaby on solo alto flute breaking through the chaos. Epic, urgent, sacred, desperate. 132 BPM, D minor. Real acoustic instruments, concert-hall reverb, no synthesizers, no pads, no electronic sounds. Loopable, instrumental, no vocals.

The hall is so large your lamps give up. Their light runs out across a floor of smooth, cracked stone and simply stops, swallowed, and the darkness beyond it goes on and on. What light there is comes up from below: violet, the color of a bruise, welling out of a thousand cracks in the floor in thin shafts that rise into the dark like the pillars of a temple that isn't there. In that light you see the real pillars. Each one is a giant, carved lying on its side, asleep, stacked one upon another all the way up into the black, a hundred sleeping stone faces gazing serenely down at you, their eyes closed.

At the center of the hall, on a bed of living rock, lies Ammaskar.

Your eyes can't take her in all at once. She's a hill. She's a ridge of the mountain that happens to have a face. She lies on her back, sixty feet from crown to heel, and she has been lying there so long that the mountain has grown over her like a blanket: moss on her shoulders, pale roots trailing over her arms, great clusters of violet crystal sprouting from the folds of her robe and glowing softly, slowly, in time with her breath. Her face is lined like a cliff and calm as deep water. Her right arm lies open at her side, palm up, and in the stone of her palm there is a socket, perfectly cut, and empty.

Kneeling beside that open hand, small as a child beside a sleeping mother, is Dorn Gultor. Grey stone covers both his arms to the shoulder now, and it's climbing his neck. He's holding the Eye against his chest in both hands, and its light pours out between his fingers, and he is trying, you can see him trying, with every muscle in his body, to set it down. His hands won't open. He's weeping. Grit falls from the ceiling like slow snow.

And the breathing stops. The whole mountain, for one long moment, holds its breath.

Soundtrack prompt · Cue · The Sleeper opens her eyes

An orchestral ambient soundtrack of an ancient giantess opening her eyes after nine hundred years of sleep, performed by a full live symphony orchestra: one long held breath of silence broken by a single deep tubular bell, then double basses, contrabassoon and tuba rising from the very bottom of the orchestra in a slow, colossal swell, divisi strings blooming above, a vast brass chorale, timpani and bass drum like a mountain shifting, building to an immense chord that hangs and does not resolve. Awe and terror. 40 BPM, C minor. Real acoustic instruments, concert-hall reverb, no synthesizers, no pads, no electronic sounds. Instrumental, no vocals.

She opens her eyes

Ammaskar's eyelids move. It takes a long time, the way the tide takes a long time, and the sound of it is a grinding that you feel in the roots of your teeth and the soles of your feet. Dust pours from her lashes in two grey waterfalls. Beneath them are eyes the size of doorways, pale and milky as moonstone, and they are not looking at anything. Not yet. They are the eyes of someone very old who has just woken in the dark and doesn't yet know where they are.

The floor of the hall lurches. A plate of stone the size of a house tilts up out of the floor with a scream of rock and slams back down. Somewhere far above you, in Bagathorn, a thousand roofs shiver at once. And beside the open hand, Dorn Gultor lifts his streaming face toward you and the Eye blazes in his fists, and his voice comes out with two voices in it, his own and something vast and slow and dreaming.

"Don't," he begs. "Please. Don't make me give it back. I'll be nothing." And the Eye, not Dorn, raises his stone hands toward you.

Roll initiative. Two dream-guardians rise from the floor beside the bed (unless the rune-token is shown). The Sleeper acts on initiative 20.

Dorn, Stone-Wed
Base: Mage (SRD) · changes below · roughly CR 10 · 5,900 XP
  • AC 16 (stone skin) · HP 150 (the mountain has mended whatever the Hushed did to him) · resistance to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing
  • Multiattack: two Dream-Shard bolts: +8 to hit, range 90 ft, 3d8 psychic (or force)
  • Stone Step (bonus action): sinks into the floor and rises from any stone within 30 ft
  • Reaction, Mountain's Shield: +5 AC against one attack
  • 1/day each (DC 16): wall of stone, flesh to stone, earthquake-lite (15-ft radius, DC 16 Dex or prone, 3d6 bludgeoning)
  • Legendary resistance (2/day): the Eye refuses to let him fail a save.
  • Can't let go: he never drops the Eye on his own. Disarming Attack, a grapple contest, or the talk-down below are the ways to get it.
The Sleeper stirs
Initiative 20 · roll d6 each round
  • 1 · Rockfall. A curtain of stone falls on a 20-ft square: DC 16 Dex, 4d10 bludgeoning, half on success (Interpose Shield works).
  • 2 · The floor heaves. Everyone standing: DC 15 Str or Dex save or prone and pushed 10 ft.
  • 3 · The dream washes out. Everyone with spellcasting: DC 15 Wis save or lose their reaction and speed until their next turn.
  • 4 · Crystal bloom. Violet crystal erupts in a 15-ft radius: difficult terrain, 2d8 piercing to anyone in it (DC 15 Dex for half).
  • 5 · Her fingers twitch. Everything within 10 ft of her open palm: DC 15 Str save or pinned (restrained, escape DC 15).
  • 6 · She breathes in. Everything not anchored is pulled 15 ft toward her face: DC 15 Str save to hold your ground. (The Immovable Rod is an anchor.)
  • Dream-guardians: 2 Earth Elementals (SRD). They attack whoever approaches her hand, unless the rune-token is shown.
  • Kolgrim (if the party won his test, from round 3): one free Greatclub attack on Dorn each round, 3d8+6.
Battlefield twistsWhat makes this fight different
TwistRuleWhy it matters
The floor is platesThe hall floor is broken into great stone plates divided by glowing fissures (see the map). When the Sleeper's "floor heaves" result comes up, one plate tilts: everyone on it slides 10 ft downhill toward the nearest fissure. A creature that slides into a fissure falls 20 ft (2d6) and needs DC 14 Athletics to climb out.Positioning matters every round. Fight on the plates near her hand, and you might be carried away from it.
The loose EyeWhenever the Eye is dropped or knocked free, at the end of each round it rolls 10 ft toward the nearest fissure, as if the mountain wants it. If it falls in, getting it back takes an action and DC 15 Athletics at the bottom (and the drink, for anyone but Boon). Mage hand (Vali has it) can carry the Eye 30 ft a turn with no drink. That's a clever play; let it work.Turns step 1 into a scramble. Boon diving for a rolling stone the whole table is shouting about is the scene.
Stone to the heart (Dorn at 75 HP)The stone reaches Dorn's heart. The floor under him rises into a 10-ft pillar with him on top: he has half cover from anyone below, climbing it is DC 14 Athletics, and he loses Stone Step. But his Dream-Shard multiattack becomes three bolts, and he gains a reaction: when a creature climbs onto the pillar, one bolt at it.A phase change halfway through, which gives melee PCs a climb and ranged PCs a target.
The guardians switch sidesHolding up the rune-token (an action) turns the two dream-guardians against Dorn for the rest of the fight.Pays off Scene 2, and gives Vali a big moment.
The talk-downBoon's action can loosen Dorn's grip (below).A combat round where the best move is a sentence.
Put her back to sleepFour steps · one action each · in orderBefore the rounds run out
StepHowWhat happens
1 · Take the Eye from Dorn built for OrekDisarming Attack (Str save vs Orek's maneuver DC) · grapple contest vs Dorn's Athletics +2 · reduce Dorn to 0 HP · or the talk-down (Boon)The Eye tumbles free across the stone. Dorn's stone stops climbing. He folds over, weeping, and stops fighting. A non-Boon hand that catches it takes the drink (see the box above).
2 · Carry it to her hand, 60 ft across heaving stone built for BoonMove it there. DC 14 Acrobatics or Athletics per 30 ft while the floor heaves (on a failure: prone, Eye dropped 10 ft away). Boon carries it with no drink.Boon: "It sits in your hand like a pebble. Everyone else who has touched it tonight has screamed."
3 · Seat it in the socket built for OrekDC 15 Investigation or jeweler's tools (Orek has advantage; auto if they found Haldra's map) · anyone else DC 18It only fits one way. On a failure, it grates and rejects, and the step can be tried again next turn.
4 · Sing her down built for ValiThe Stone-Lullaby in Giant: auto if Thrunna taught it · else DC 15 Performance or Persuasion (Vali: advantage, he's kin; Orek speaks Giant) · advantage if Thrunna is singing too (round 3+)Read "She sleeps."
Talk Dorn downBoon only · an actionDC 16 Persuasion or Intimidation · advantage if they found the journal

Your brother is turning to stone, begging you not to make him ordinary. You're the only person in the world who knows what he's afraid of. What do you say?

Success

Dorn stares at you. The stone has reached his jaw; it cracks when he speaks. "You lived," he whispers. "Thirty years in a cell, and no magic, and you lived." Something in his face gives way. His fingers, one by one, as if each one weighs as much as the mountain, begin to open. The Eye's light spills out between them. "Take it. Boon. Please. Take it before I can't."

Step 1 succeeds automatically on the next attempt, and Dorn doesn't resist it.

Failure

"Don't you dare." The Eye flares in his fists and his voice goes huge, two voices, his and hers. "Don't you dare pity me. You were always the one who didn't matter. You don't get to be the one who's right."

Dorn targets Boon with everything next turn. Boon can try again.

Round 3 · the giants come optional

Far across the hall, a section of wall slides aside, and Thrunna Stonesinger steps through it, ducking under a lintel built for someone even larger than she is, with Kolgrim behind her. They don't hurry. They don't fight. Thrunna sees her grandmother's open eyes and stops, and something passes over her ancient face that you have no word for. Then she opens her mouth, and sings: the four lines, low and patient, over and over. The floor under your feet steadies, just a little, the way a frightened horse steadies under a hand it knows.

From now on, step 4 has advantage. If Kolgrim was singing the mountain down (clock-7 effect), Thrunna strikes him once across the face, hard, and he stops.

She sleeps

The Eye settles into Ammaskar's palm with a sound you will remember for the rest of your life: a small, clean click, like a key turning in a lock that has waited nine hundred years for it. Light floods back into it, violet and slow, the fish under the ice beginning to swim again. And the song goes up, the four lines, in a goliath's voice or a dwarf's, and Thrunna's under it, and Kolgrim's, grudging, and the hall takes the song and makes it enormous.

Ammaskar's great fingers close around the Eye. Gently. The way a sleeping child's hand closes around a finger. Her moonstone eyes drift across the hall, slowly, and find you, a cluster of small warm figures with lamps at her side. For one moment she looks at you, and you feel it: a mind as wide and slow as the mountain, a vast, drowsy, puzzled curiosity, as if she is trying to remember whether she dreamed you or you dreamed her.

Then she sighs. It's a wind that goes through the whole hall, warm and smelling of stone and moss and something sweet, and every lamp you carry gutters and flares. Her eyelids slide down, grinding, slow as the tide going out. The violet crystals on her shoulders dim, and brighten, and dim, and settle into the slow, long rhythm of somebody who is, once again, very deeply asleep. The floor stops moving. Grit stops falling. And somewhere very far above you, in a town on a mountain's shoulder, a thousand lanterns slow, and slow, and hang still.

If dawn comes first

Ammaskar sits up. It begins at her shoulders, a groan that comes from everywhere at once, and the bed of living rock cracks across like bread, and the sleeping giants carved into the pillars crack with it, and the whole hall tilts. Up and up she comes, a hill unfolding, moss and crystal pouring from her like water off a surfacing whale, and far above you the mountain, the town, the Gultor Tower, a thousand roofs, all of it rises with her chest.

And on Boon's wrist the bracelet goes cold, and burns, and pulls. The Gate. Dawn. Seraphine's voice, calm, in all your ears at once: "Hands on the convict, Detectives. Now." Whoever is touching Boon goes with him. The hall folds sideways into grey. The last thing you see is a vast, pale, puzzled face turning toward the place where you were, as the ceiling comes down like rain.

You land on the cold floor of the Gate chamber in the Nexus in a heap, coughing grit. Somebody's lamp is still lit. Above you, the clerk at the lever checks her ledger, and checks it again, and very quietly makes a mark in the column marked failed.

Fail forward: most of Bagathorn had already climbed the pass road; the upper tiers and the Gultor Tower are gone. Dorn's fate is whatever the party did to him before the recall (anyone not touching Boon is left behind: Seraphine sends a retrieval team, and they turn up a day later, alive and very angry). Bagathorn's Grudge +2. Skip to "Come home" and change Seraphine's line to "Contract failed. The client, I'm told, survived. He'll want to speak with you."

sections.title: Dawn
sections.html:
☼

Dawn

SunriseThe Hall of Ammaskar → Lantern Square → the Nexus
Who: Thrunna, Dorn, Bramm, Fennick, Ragna and Tam, Mayor Durrin, SeraphineLeans on: one closing beat for each PC
Soundtrack prompt · Dawn

An orchestral ambient soundtrack of sunrise over a dwarven mountain town that has survived the night, performed by a live chamber orchestra: the giants' simple lullaby melody returning, now on warm solo cello, then passed to solo oboe and to gentle French horn, over soft sustained strings and rippling concert harp, a quiet glockenspiel like light catching frost, a slow swell of the full strings as the sun clears the ridge. Weary, tender, hopeful, a little bittersweet. 64 BPM, G major. Real acoustic instruments, concert-hall reverb, no synthesizers, no pads, no electronic sounds. Loopable, instrumental, no vocals.

Judgment Vali

Dorn sits against the bed of living rock with his grey arms in his lap, and doesn't look up. The stone stopped climbing the moment the Eye left his hands; it has reached his jaw and gone no further, and it won't go back. When he tries to light a cantrip, out of habit, nothing happens. Nothing will, ever again. He laughs, a small dry sound, and stops.

Thrunna kneels, which takes a long time, and puts her face near his, and breathes in. "Ink," she says. "And weeping. This is the one." She turns her river-stone eyes, not to the dwarves, but to the goliath. "Cousin. You believe the ones who do harm must answer for it. So do we. The pact says he is ours, to give to the stone. But you put her back to sleep." She waits. "Say what you think is just, and I will listen."

Dorn goes to…What it means
The stone (the giants' law)Thrunna lays him in the wall of the hall, and the rock closes over him like a blanket. He'll dream for a hundred years. "When he wakes he will be wiser, or he will be stone." Bramm weeps and doesn't object.
IroncladSeraphine, in their ears: "Bring him. A man who knows what it is to lose his gift. A man who knows where the giants sleep. We always need strays." Dorn gets a bracelet. He'll be in the cell next to Boon's. (The giants accept if Vali asks: "Small ones' justice is shorter. Perhaps that is crueler.")
Bagathorn's jailMayor Durrin gets the public trial he wanted and makes a meal of it. The town learns the whole truth, including the old bomb.
FreedomThrunna doesn't like it. Bagathorn's Grudge +1, and the giants trust the pact less. Dorn walks up the pass road alone and is never seen in Bagathorn again.

Come up into the morning

Haldra's stair, or the giants' road, or the long cage out of the Ninth Gallery: it's a long way up, and none of you speaks much. Then there's daylight. Real daylight, thin and gold and freezing, pouring over the eastern ridge and down the mountain's shoulder, and Bagathorn lies below you in it, tier on tier, every roof still standing. The lanterns in the square hang perfectly still.

And up the pass road, the long river of lamps is coming back. Slowly. A family at a time. A woman with two children on her hips. A boy of eight pulling a smaller girl along by the hand. Mules and carts and grandmothers and a man carrying a clock. Someone in Lantern Square has started ringing the bronze bell again, not in short nervous bursts now, but steadily, on and on, the way you'd ring it for a wedding.

Closing beats

Boon · Bramm and Ragna

Bramm meets them in the square and puts a heavy, battered workbook into Boon's hands: "This was always yours. They had no right to take it, and I had no right to keep it." If Dorn is gone: "Haldra's word needs a keeper. Fennick will do it if you won't. But it should be offered to you first." Then Ragna, if Tam lived and she's seen the journal: she says nothing at all. She holds out a brass miner's lamp, old, dented, polished to a shine, with 12 stamped on its base. Olin's. She puts it in Boon's hands and walks away.

Orek · Stone-Setter

Thrunna, before she goes down: "You set her Eye the way a cutter sets a stone. Not with magic. With your hands and your eye." She gives him a name in Giant, Ostvaer, Stone-Setter, and asks whether the small ones have a better one for him. Whatever he answers is what the giants of Dhurak-Ul will call him forever. (And there's still a letter from Yardim Opaldigger in his pocket.)

Vali · Waking Cousin

Old Hagga, who hasn't spoken all night, opens one great eye as the party passes the pithead, and speaks one word in Giant to Vali: "Thorvald." Waking Cousin. The one of their blood who walks in the dream and remembers that it's real. Thrunna lets him keep the rune-token. "Come back, cousin. Come down and sit with her sometime. She would like to dream you."

Soundtrack prompt · Cue · Come home, Detectives

An orchestral ambient soundtrack of tired detectives stepping back through a dimensional gate into a strange interplanar headquarters after a hard case, performed by a full live symphony orchestra: a harp glissando and shimmering tremolo violins opening the gate, then the cool noir theme on solo clarinet returning over walking pizzicato basses and brushed snare, a muted trumpet answering, and a final soft, wry chord on low strings and celesta. Weary, satisfied, mysterious. 76 BPM, D Dorian. Real acoustic instruments, concert-hall reverb, no synthesizers, no pads, no electronic sounds. Instrumental, no vocals.

Come home

At the exact moment the sun clears the ridge, the air in the middle of Lantern Square tears open like wet paper, and through the gap blows the smell of ozone and parchment dust and clockwork grease. A small boy in a blanket points at it and shrieks with delight. On Boon's wrist, the bracelet gives one small click: asset, becoming prisoner.

You step through. Grey, and falling sideways, and then the cold stone of the Gate chamber under your boots and the Astral Sea pouring violet light down the spiral stair. Turnkey Nine is waiting at the bottom of it with the shackles. Above you, on a floating walkway, a clerk is already writing.

And in your ears, all three, cool and close: "The asset is secure. Contract complete." A pause, long enough that you think she's gone. Then, so quietly you almost miss it: "Good work, Detectives."

Cliffhanger · the closed eye

Turnkey Nine walks Boon back to the cells the long way, through the Nexus Bazaar, because the lift is broken again. The Bazaar never closes. Stalls of brass and silk and bone crowd the walkways, selling things from a hundred worlds: a jar of bottled thunder, a map that redraws itself, a box that whispers when you open it.

In the third ring there's a stall nobody seems to be looking at. Its awning is black, its counter bare, and painted over it, small and neat, is a closed eye. The stall is empty. Packed up in a hurry: a scatter of silver wire on the boards, a smear of black wax. But there's a card pinned to the counter, and written on it in an elegant hand, a name. Yours.

Handout · pinned to the counter of the closed-eye stall
Mister Gultor,
Your brother paid me with a ring three hundred years old. Lamp and giant, very fine.
Your family has sold me other things, over the years. Come and see what else I have of yours.
— C.
Corvane's Card
Loot · gear

An invitation, or a threat. Starts the Corvane thread for the next Ironclad case.

Variations

The miners diedRagna is at the square at dawn with four lamps in her arms, and she doesn't look at anyone. No lamp for Boon. Grudge +2.
The journal was never foundBramm still says "I never believed you drew it wrong." Boon gets half the truth. The journal stays in the desk for a future case.
Boon carried the EyeThrunna, to Boon: "The dry one. The one she couldn't drink. Haldra was dry too, they say." (A seed: was the first pact-keeper like Boon?)

After the session

  • Series clocks: Corvane (+1 per trigger in the arc doc) · Bagathorn's Grudge
  • Ledger: Dorn's fate · the miners · who keeps Haldra's word · the receipt
  • Loot: sliver, Hush, rune-token, charges, workbook, journal, Olin's lamp, Corvane's card
  • Fee: 4,000 gp to Ironclad; 600 gp per Detective [OPEN]
  • Ask Eddy what Vali's patron thought of the Sleeper's flinch

dream-guardian.token: A dream-guardian: a tall humanoid figure of smooth dark granite half-stepping out of a rune-carved wall, faint opalescent violet runes glowing across its chest and arms, its face a calm featureless mask with closed, sleeping eyes. Serene, ancient and immovable.

traits.name: Earth Glide
traits.text: The earth elemental can burrow through nonmagical, unworked earth and stone. While doing so, the earth elemental doesn't disturb the material it moves through.

traits.name: Siege Monster
traits.text: The earth elemental deals double damage to objects and structures.

stone-servant.notes: Pulled out of the apron by Kolgrim’s note. Tries to shove PCs out of the ring and into the coal-cart fire. Crumbles to gravel the moment Kolgrim yields.
stone-servant.token: A stone servant: a blunt, crude humanoid heaved up out of rough grey rock and coal-dust gravel, no face at all, lumpy shoulders, arms like broken columns, loose stones trickling from its joints. Heavy, mindless and obedient.

kolgrim.notes: A ritual, not a murder. Yields at 100 HP and sits down hard; the servants collapse. A PC dropped to 0 is stable. Lost if the party yields or two of them are down. Opens with the boulder at whoever looks smallest; saves Vali-in-Large-Form for last.
kolgrim.token: Kolgrim, a young stone giant: hulking and broad, skin of grey granite with pale quartz flecks, a heavy jaw split by a big delighted laugh, dark hair in thick braids threaded with river stones, a boulder the size of a cart balanced on one shoulder. Coal dust and firelight. Boisterous, proud and itching for a fight.

hushed.name: The Hushed

traits.name: Evasion
traits.text: If the assassin is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, the assassin instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the save and only half damage if it fails. It can't use this trait if it has the Incapacitated condition.

traits.name: Hush of the Deep
traits.text: The Hushed makes no sound and has Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. A creature with Tremorsense (Boon, Orek with Stonecunning) still feels its steps on stone.

actions.name: Shortsword
actions.text: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) Piercing damage plus 17 (5d6) Poison damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the start of the assassin's next turn.

actions.name: Light Crossbow
actions.text: Ranged Attack Roll: +7, range 80/320 ft. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) Piercing damage plus 21 (6d6) Poison damage.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.text: The assassin makes three attacks, using Shortsword or Light Crossbow in any combination.

bonus.name: Cunning Action
bonus.text: The assassin takes the Dash, the Disengage, or Hide action.

hushed.notes: Corvane’s agents. They want the Eye, not the party: round 1, one goes for Dorn. Grabbing the Eye burns them too (3d10 Psychic), so they try to drag Dorn to the slit. At the end of round 3 the stone takes Dorn; survivors fight one more round, then go out the slit on grapnels. A captured one talks (DC 15 Intimidation).
hushed.token: One of the Hushed, a silent assassin: slim figure in close-fitting charcoal leathers and a deep hood, face hidden behind a smooth pale porcelain mask with no mouth, one gloved finger raised to where the lips would be, a thin blackened shortsword. Eerie, quiet and deadly.

dorn.name: Dorn, Stone-Wed

actions.name: Dream-Shard
actions.text: Ranged Spell Attack Roll: +8, range 90 ft. Hit: 13 (3d8) Psychic damage.

actions.name: Wall of Stone (1/Day)
actions.text: Dorn casts Wall of Stone (spell save DC 16).

actions.name: Flesh to Stone (1/Day)
actions.text: Dorn casts Flesh to Stone (spell save DC 16).

actions.name: The Mountain Shrugs (1/Day)
actions.text: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 16, each creature in a 15-foot-radius Sphere Dorn can see. Failure: 10 (3d6) Bludgeoning damage and the target has the Prone condition. Success: Half damage only.

bonus.name: Stone Step
bonus.text: Dorn sinks into the floor and rises from any stone within 30 feet.

reactions.name: Mountain’s Shield
reactions.text: Trigger: Dorn is hit by an attack roll. Response: +5 AC against that attack.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (2/Day)
traits.text: If Dorn fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead. The Eye refuses to let him fail.

traits.name: Can’t Let Go
traits.text: Dorn never drops the Eye on his own. Disarming Attack, a grapple contest (his Athletics +2), dropping him to 0 HP or Boon’s talk-down are the ways to get it. Taking the Eye ends his fight.

traits.name: Stone to the Heart
traits.text: At 75 HP the floor raises Dorn on a 10-foot pillar: half cover from below, DC 14 Athletics to climb, he loses Stone Step, Dream-Shard becomes three bolts, and he gains a Reaction to bolt anyone who climbs on.

dorn.notes: Mage reskin (CR ~10). Doesn’t have to die: taking the Eye from him ends his fight. Kolgrim (if his test was won) gets one free Greatclub hit on him each round from round 3: 3d8 + 6.
dorn.token: Dorn Gultor, Stone-Wed: a handsome dwarf wizard half turned to living stone, grey stone veins climbing from his throat across one side of his face, his braided beard beaded with silver, a torn deep-blue velvet coat, and a fist-sized black gem with moving violet lights blazing through the cloth over his heart. Terrified and furious.
